title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model
snippet: Nvidia just released a free speech-to-text model that can transcribe up to 40 languages, but it only works on recordings, not live audio, so it’s a big step for meeting and medical transcription tools while still leaving real-time use to rivals like ElevenLabs.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

8:00 AM PDT · October 28, 2026

Image Credits:TechCrunch/AI generated

		

							

											
									

					

	

Nvidia on Wednesday released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages. It also released version 2 of Granary, its open-source speech dataset.

Nvidia boasts that Nemotron 3.5 can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, and tell up to eight speakers apart. It claims to beat rivals on benchmarks, including Hugging Face’s Open ASR Leaderboard.

These tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription, two of AI’s most established footholds in the workplace. Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset, and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customize apps to recognize an industry’s jargon in each language. One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not live streams.

Still, the company promises Transcribe, at 30 billion parameters, can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and DGX Spark chip powering new laptops, to Blackwell datacenter chips. It joins Nvidia’s open-weight voice models, including the super small yet powerful Parakeet (1.1 billion parameters).

Nvidia’s latest voice entry comes during busy period of AI voice releases: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 earlier this month; ElevenLabs launched Realtime for instant speech in voice agents; and Salesforce released Launa-Omni, its voice model.

title: Free Fire returns to India as Garena launches localized version four years after ban
snippet: Free Fire India was originally set to launch in September 2023, but Garena postponed its release.
fullText:
More than four years after New Delhi banned Free Fire over national security concerns, Garena has brought the popular battle royale game back to India with a localized version.

On Wednesday, Garena launched the localized version, called Free Fire India, as a standalone game available on Android and iOS. The new version features India-specific content, parental controls, playtime limits, and spending caps, with user data hosted on servers in India, the firm owned by Southeast Asian giant Sea said. The launch comes more than three years after Garena quietly postponed Free Fire India’s earlier release after announcing it in September 2023.

Free Fire was one of India’s most popular mobile games before it was banned in February 2022 alongside 53 other apps over alleged links to China. The game had become more popular after India banned its rival PUBG Mobile in September 2020. Free Fire’s ban, however, sent shares of Singapore-based Sea, Garena’s parent company, tumbling, wiping more than $16 billion off its market value in a single day. Still, Garena remained active in India. Free Fire MAX, an enhanced version of the game, was not among the banned apps and remained available to players.

PUBG Mobile’s South Korean publisher Krafton later introduced Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI), a version similar to PUBG Mobile but made specifically for Indian players. But BGMI has struggled to match the popularity of Garena’s Free Fire franchise. In June, the franchise had about 77.4 million monthly active users in India, compared with 20.8 million for BGMI, according to Sensor Tower data reviewed by TechCrunch.

Vaibhav Das Mundhra, Garena’s head of operations in India, told TechCrunch that Free Fire MAX would remain available alongside Free Fire India. Players will be able to use the same account across both games, play together and take part in the same events, he said.

Garena, Mundhra said, had worked with relevant Indian government authorities and incorporated their feedback while preparing Free Fire India for launch. However, he did not answer questions about why the game’s planned 2023 launch was delayed or what had changed to allow its release now.

While Free Fire India’s launch remained on hold, TechCrunch earlier reported that Garena continued developing games for the Indian market. Through its studios in Pune and Mumbai, the company worked on titles inspired by Hindu mythology, cricket, and the traditional board game Ludo, releasing some of them while the original Free Fire remained banned. One of those titles, Versus, was previously available in early access on Google Play but is no longer listed on the store.

Despite regulatory setbacks, India remains a significant market for mobile gaming companies. Mobile game downloads in the country grew 14.2% quarter-over-quarter to 2 billion in Q2, while revenue rose 3.7% to more than $106 million, per Sensor Tower.

Garena’s Free Fire MAX has also maintained a presence in India’s esports scene, with Indian teams including S8UL Esports, Apex Gaming, and Total Gaming competing at the Esports World Cup 2026.

Animesh Agarwal, co-founder and CEO of S8UL Esports, said Free Fire India’s return could open up more opportunities for players and creators. “For me, the real impact goes beyond the game itself. It’s about the players who dream of building a career in esports, the creators who have built communities around the title, and the opportunities this ecosystem can create for everyone involved,” he said.

title: AT&T Is Paying Out Its $177 Million Data Breach Settlement. You Might Get a Check Soon
snippet: If you filed a claim by Dec. 18, 2025, a check for up to $7,500 could be on its way within the next few months.
fullText:
Over 110 million AT&T customers had their personal information stolen in two high-profile data breaches during 2019 and 2024. The cybersecurity incidents exposed sensitive data, prompting consumers to seek compensation through a class-action lawsuit.

The lawsuit (PDF) alleged that AT&T didn’t do enough to protect customer data or to promptly notify them of the data breaches. While the company didn’t admit to any wrongdoing, it agreed to pay $177 million in restitution to the settlement class.

The deadline to file a claim was last December, but these settlement transactions take a long time to process. Money must be divided to cover administrative and legal fees. Information must also be disseminated to as many eligible settlement class members as possible.

			

More from CNET

More than 4.9 million eligible customers filed a claim, and you may be one of them. 

Though AT&T can still appeal the court’s decision until Nov. 2, if no appeal is made, the court has 10 days to issue a final approval for the settlement. The payouts would then be issued electronically or by mail within 60 days of that final approval (PDF), meaning claimants could potentially receive their settlement money by early 2027.

How much money can you expect from the AT&T settlement?

If you filed a valid claim as part of the AT&T data breach settlement and provided documentation of financial losses, you could be eligible to receive up to $7,500, depending on the settlement class you’re a part of (PDF). Here’s how that breaks down. 

2019 breach: As part of the AT&T 1 Data Incident settlement class, anyone whose Social Security number was stolen and who can prove they suffered financial losses from the hack is eligible for up to a $5,000 check.

2024 breach: As part of the AT&T 2 Data Incident settlement class, anyone who proved they suffered financial loss in relation to this hack is eligible for up to a $2,500 check.

Customers who could prove they were affected by the AT&T 1 and AT&T 2 breaches are eligible for up to a $7,500 check, provided they have documentation for both breaches.

However, the vast bulk of eligible claimants — more than 3.7 million — who did not include any documentation of losses with their claim forms will get drastically lower payouts in what’s called a tiered distribution system. The tiered cash payments are far below the settlement’s advertised maximums, ranging from $6.50 to $40. These claims will be paid out “pro rata,” meaning the money will be distributed evenly based on what’s left in the total settlement allotment. 

All payout amounts are estimates and not guaranteed. 

If you filed a claim and want more information or updates, you can contact the settlement administrator on the website telecomdatasettlement.com or by calling 833-890-4930. 

The hackers behind the 2024 AT&T hack are closely associated with the infamous ShinyHunters group.Timon Schneider/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty Images

What happened during the 2019 and 2024 data breaches?

AT&T suffered two major data breaches in 2019 and 2024, with customers’ personal information appearing on the dark web after the latter incident. The company did not publicly acknowledge the hack for several weeks after the leaked data began proliferating online.

The 2019 hack affected 65.4 million former customers and 7.6 million active account holders, exposing extremely sensitive information including Social Security numbers, birth dates and full legal names. The leaked information was important and wide-ranging enough that AT&T took the drastic measure of resetting the passwords of every affected customer.

The 2024 breach was broader in scope, impacting nearly 109 million wireless customers, but the information wasn’t as sensitive. During this hack, call and text records, timestamps and cell tower location data that AT&T had saved from 2022 were illegally accessed. 

(Because nearly all 73 million people from the first breach were also part of the broader 110 million pool in the second breach, the total number of customers affected is capped at around 110 million.)

Hackers from the UNC5537 group claimed responsibility for the 2024 breach, part of a larger hacking spree targeting the Snowflake databases of more than 160 companies. UNC5537is a close affiliate of ShinyHunters, a notorious hacker group that frequently targets corporations with large stores of customer information. Two individuals were arrested in connection with the case.

While the exploits used in 2024 have been thoroughly documented and patched, hackers continue to target Snowflake servers through third-party partners, as seen in the recent Rockstar server hack.

title: Anthropic is printing money, but AI isn’t paying off outside tech

fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m reading about Netflix’s bloody week, playing with Apple Music’s fun new 404 page, mourning Arc’s untimely demise, and devouring Maggie O’Farrell’s new novel, Land.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

Anthropic is going public, and thanks to its S-1, we now have access to some of the mouthwatering numbers behind the IPO. In the first half of the year, the company reported $16.3 billion in revenue, up from $1.2 billion for the same period of 2025. If you’ve been following the AI phenomenon at all, you’ll know why: Anthropic’s Claude Code kicked off the AI coding boom in early 2026, causing every company from Google to OpenAI to largely pivot to the enterprise. By the summer we were talking about “token-maxxing” as Claude Fable 5.1 ate billions of tokens every day.

	

With a rumored valuation approaching $1.5 trillion, Anthropic’s IPO, when it does happen, will be the largest of all time, eclipsing SpaceXAI’s by billions of dollars. The interesting thing about the numbers, at least to me, is how much cash is on hand: of the $141 billion raised so far, it has over $112 billion remaining.

However, Anthropic has committed to spending hundreds of billions of dollars with Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and SpaceX for cloud infrastructure, and expects to be compute-constrained over the next year. All of the major hyperscalers, including Google, have are prioritizing their own AI workloads over competitors’, meaning that Anthropic will be on the hunt for newer and potentially less reliable providers, with data centers largely powered by natural gas to keep costs down.

The data in this prospectus are truly outrageous. Anthropic did not exist until 2021 and was largely seen as an ideological research outfit until fairly recently. The notion that it would be one of the hottest stocks of ever was laughable, but here we are.

Conversely, a viral post by Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok last week is making the argument that except for tech, AI is not moving the needle.

In a number of compelling charts, Slok outlines the fact that while the Magnificent 7 are propping up the US economy, the rest of the country’s largest businesses — the S&P 493, as he calls them — are not seeing rising profits or meaningful productivity gains. 

“Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence,” it begins, “the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech. There are still no signs of AI boosting productivity growth.”

Perhaps most concerning is where AI spend is concentrated: 80% of the top 1% of all AI spenders in the US are VC-backed companies, reinforcing the idea that frontier models are still the darlings of Silicon Valley more than Main Street.

Ultimately, both things can be true: the AI labs are minting money, but most other businesses haven’t seen the returns.

Welcome to Cc:, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. This week, I’m speaking with C. Scott Brown, a video creator at Android Authority and on his own channel.

Who are you?

C. Scott Brown

What do you do for work?

I’m a video creator at Android Authority and on my solo channel, C. Scott Brown (clever name, I know).

What do you do for fun?

I enjoy cycling and hiking quite a bit. I spend a lot of time with my partner watching movies, too, as we’re both big film buffs.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

Technology has always been a huge part of my life. I really love it. I love when a piece of technology makes my life better/easier, even if only in a small way. I genuinely believe that technology is what moves humanity forward.

What are three apps you can’t live without and why?

The Homey app is so important to me because my entire smart home runs through my Homey Pro, and I don’t even know what my life would look like without it. I’m also addicted to Reddit, and the Relay app is my way of accessing it, so I open it about 400 times a day. Finally, the Tautulli app keeps me hooked into what’s going on with my Plex server, so I check that a lot each day, too.

What is a gadget that you love right now?

I just got done reviewing the Fitbit Edge. I really like the Edge, but while reviewing it, I had to set my Pixel Watch 5 aside for the week. Now that the Edge review is done, I am very, very happy to have my Pixel Watch 5 back!

How does AI fit into your life right now?

I use AI to solve many practical problems in my life. Being a video creator involves a lot of small, mind-numbing tasks, and AI helps me do them faster or, in some cases, remove them entirely from my plate. However, I will never use AI to take over any creative aspects of my job. That’s the fun stuff!

What’s a book you recently read and loved?

The YouTube Formula by Derral Eves. I’m still learning so much about YouTube and how to improve my videos, and this book has been very helpful. I just wish it was written a bit better (sorry, Derral).

What’s an album (or two) you recently listened to and loved?

My two favorite albums of 2026 so far are Get Mean by Boy Harsher and Fantasia by Slift. I love the minimalist simplicity of Boy Harsher’s music. They’ve locked into a vibe and just beat it into the ground. They’re like the AC/DC of synthwave. Meanwhile, Slift is such an amazing band, and it’s so refreshing to hear loud rock music that isn’t overproduced, radio-friendly, or trying to fit into a modern scene. Fantasia is just guitars cranked up to 11, screaming vocals, pounding drums, and everything else I’ve ever loved about loud music.

What’s a TV show you recently watched and loved?

I mean, the only answer in 2026 is Widow’s Bay. It’s literally perfect. Perfect cast, perfect storylines, funny when it needs to be, just enough scares, terrific drama…there’s nothing to dislike about it.

What’s a movie you recently watched and loved?

Everyone Is Lying to You for Money was a banger. It was preaching to the choir for me because I’ve always known crypto was a giant sham, but even if we set that aside, the film was immensely enjoyable and way funnier than I expected.

What’s a game you recently played and loved?

Dungeons of Hinterberg was one of my recent discoveries. It was like Persona meets Zelda with a millennial going through an existential crisis. It sounds awful when I write it out like that, but I thought it was terrific!

What’s something offline you do every day that brings you joy?

Drink a cup of tea. Or three or four cups. It is the simplest and most effective way to make me happy.

➡️ FWD:

Here’s a less cheerful follow-up to last week’s foldable excitement: some iPhone Duo owners are reporting cracked inner screens. Teardowns have raised possible explanations involving pressure from the hinge mechanism, which JerryRigEverything tries to prove in his latest video.

Apple has now acknowledged the issue is affecting “a small number” of units and says owners should contact AppleCare for a replacement. Still, however small the number, it’s likely to tarnish Apple’s big launch in some way, and it certainly won’t help dispel the belief that foldables are just too fragile for the mainstream.

🗑️ Trash

Google has updated its privacy policy to allow for the possibility of using Gmail and Photos data to personalize ads. Anyone who’s enabled Gemini’s Personal Intelligence feature (and if you want it to be useful, you should be) now agrees to allow Google to “access data from other Google services you use, such as Google Photos and Workspace apps, in order to provide you with a more personalized experience, subject to the policies and settings of the accessing service.”

I’m not surprised about this change; anonymized Gmail and Photos data is like crack for advertisers, and Google has finally found a way to justify utilizing it. Yes, if a service is free, then you’re the product, but Google is also asking you to pay a lot of money for Gemini, so the bargain doesn’t feel as fair anymore.

title: Vivo’s X500 series launches globally with MediaTek chips and insane cameras
snippet: Following its initial debut in China, Vivo is officially taking its flagship lineup global. The X500 series brings three new models to the international stage, including the Vivo X500, X500 Pro, and the range-topping X500 Pro Max. more…
fullText:
Following its initial debut in China, Vivo is officially taking its flagship lineup global. The X500 series brings three new models to the international stage, including the Vivo X500, X500 Pro, and the range-topping X500 Pro Max.

What’s interesting is that the Chinese OEM has just jumped straight past the X400 to the X500, for what reason, we’re not entirely sure. This is a direct follow-on from the X300 lineup, which was released earlier this year and has been such a promising lineup.

Under the hood, both the X500 Pro and Pro Max are powerhouses, becoming the first smartphones to feature MediaTek’s new 2nm Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset. The standard X500 is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 9600M. Display-wise, both Pro models sport 2K 144Hz BOE Q11 LTPO AMOLED displays—6.36-inch on the Pro and 6.85-inch on the Pro Max—reaching up to 4,500 nits peak brightness. The vanilla X500 sits in the middle with a 6.59-inch 144Hz AMOLED screen.

Battery capacities have taken a massive leap forward across the board thanks to high-density silicon-carbon technology: an 8,000 mAh cell inside the Pro Max, 6,510 mAh in the Pro, and 7,500 mAh in the standard X500. All three models support 90W wired FlashCharge and 40W wireless charging, carry dual IP68 & IP69 water and dust resistance, and ship running OriginOS 7 based on Android 17.

	

But as expected, the cameras are the (pun intended…) main focus here.

Co-engineered with Zeiss, the X500 Pro and Pro Max center around a custom 50MP 24mm-equivalent main sensor (Sony LYTIA L910, 1/1.28-inch) featuring an f/1.57 aperture, Zeiss T* coating, and 17 EV of dynamic range. The Pro Max features a “gimbal-grade” 3-degree OIS setup, while the Pro steps back slightly to 1.5 degrees.

For zoom, the X500 Pro Max packs an 85mm-equivalent 200MP periscope telephoto (Samsung ISOCELL HP0, 1/1.4-inch) backed by CIPA 7.0 pro-grade stabilization. The X500 Pro uses a custom 85mm-equivalent 64MP telephoto (Sony LYTIA 610, 1/2.0-inch) with the same stabilization rating. Both Pro variants share a 15mm-equivalent 50MP ISOCELL JN5 ultrawide lens and support an optional 400mm-equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 Ultra add-on lens. The company has banked on Pro photography kits in recent years, and this is yet another device shipping with an option.

Meanwhile, the base vivo X500 features a 23mm 50MP LYTIA 828 main camera, a 72mm 64MP telephoto, and a 50MP ISOCELL JN1 ultrawide shooter.

Video performance gets a serious upgrade, too. The X500 Pro and Pro Max offer 4K 240fps cinematic slow motion, 10-bit video capture with 422 encoding, and ACES (Academy Color Encoding System) support, while the Pro Max tops out with 8K 30fps recording and 4K 120fps Pro AF Tracking Video.

As for aesthetics, the standard Vivo X500 comes in White, Gray, Black, and Pink. The X500 Pro and X500 Pro Max are offered in White, Gray, Black, and a standout Sunset Orange finish. The White, Gray, and Orange finishes feature a subtle micro-dot shimmer, while the Black option features a pyramid-like light-shifting texture. 

At the time of publishing, Rrgional pricing and localized availability dates for specific global markets will be confirmed soon. We’ll update once available.

title: Apple Creator Studio gets powerful new AI features using OpenAI models
snippet: Apple Creator Studio updates have today been announced, with what the company describes as “powerful new AI features” using a combination of Apple Intelligence and OpenAI models. Final Cut Pro for Mac will also include built-in MotionVFX to provide a large collection of visual effects, transitions, and motion graphics tools … more…
fullText:
Apple Creator Studio updates have today been announced, with what the company describes as “powerful new AI features” using a combination of Apple Intelligence and OpenAI models.

Final Cut Pro for Mac will also include built-in MotionVFX to provide a large collection of visual effects, transitions, and motion graphics tools … 

Apple announced the updates alongside the new iMacs and 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip. It will be a free update for existing subscribers at some point in November.

Final Cut Pro for Mac now includes built-in MotionVFX — an expansive collection of visual effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates, and motion graphics tools — as well as seamless editing in Pixelmator Pro. Apple’s curated Content Hub now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro.

Music creators using Logic Pro for Mac gain a new intelligent assistant in beta, an enhanced Stem Splitter that now separates drums, and a redesigned Browser that incorporates all sounds, with music understanding and even a Splice library.

Pixelmator Pro introduces Generate Fill, which lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language.

Keynote, Pages, and Numbers introduce new AI features in beta, including assistants2 that understand document context and new Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for workflow automation. They also add stock video in the Content Hub and new premium themes and templates.

The headline news here is MotionVFX for Final Cut Pro.

Final Cut Pro for Mac now integrates MotionVFX directly into the app, giving editors access to thousands of elements, including templates with unique themes, stylish graphics, titles, and transitions, as well as tools for rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading. Editors can also tap into the Content Hub directly within Final Cut Pro and access a library of Apple-curated stock videos, photos, and backgrounds to fill gaps, add polish, or spark new ideas without leaving their workflow.

Also notable is that the inclusion of OpenAI models alongside Apple Intelligence.

A new intelligent assistant powered by a combination of Apple-built models and OpenAI joins Logic Pro for Mac, helping creators and producers navigate production workflows, start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project.

and:

Visual productivity apps receive a new generation of intelligence features for subscribers, including an intelligent assistant, built on Apple models and OpenAI, directly within Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. The assistant understands document context to help users accomplish more without leaving their work.

In Keynote, the intelligent assistant helps with designing, animating, and refining slides. In Pages, it drafts, restructures, and fine-tunes written content. In Numbers, it calculates, visualizes, and organizes data; recommends suitable chart types with a one-tap preview; and builds custom tables using world knowledge.

New MCP support, built on this platform, enables external AI agents and tools to read content, perform edits, and execute automated actions directly in Keynote, Pages, and Numbers.

Apple hasn’t announced an exact launch date for the new features, instead saying that it will be “this November.”

title: Ollama for Mac gains support for local text-to-speech models
snippet: Ollama, the popular app for running AI models locally, announced that its Mac app now supports text-to-speech generation, with Windows and Linux support coming soon. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Ollama, the popular app for running AI models locally, announced that its Mac app now supports text-to-speech generation, with Windows and Linux support coming soon. Here are the details.

Ollama now supports speech models

If you’re not familiar with Ollama, it is a platform that lets users download and run open AI models locally on their Macs, or access more powerful models through the cloud. It is also available for Windows and Linux.

Ollama itself is open-source and has become one of the most popular AI projects on GitHub, with nearly 185,000 stars and around 18,600 forks. You can learn more about it here.

On macOS, Ollama uses Apple’s MLX, an open-source machine learning framework that leverages Apple Silicon’s unified memory architecture, enabling supported AI models to run faster and more efficiently.

Once users get Ollama up and running, they can download compatible open-source AI models from repositories such as Hugging Face and run them directly on their Macs.

This means they can use AI without an internet connection or sending their data to external servers, although performance and the size of the models they can run depend heavily on their Mac’s hardware.

That said, Ollama recently announced support for Phonon, a family of text-to-speech models developed by Gradium, marking the first time the platform supports speech generation.

As Ollama explains, speech is generated in real time, meaning users can listen to AI-generated responses as they’re being produced, rather than waiting for the entire response to finish.

From Ollama:

Ollama can now turn text into speech. The first speech model is Phonon, a family of small, state-of-the-art text-to-speech models from Gradium. Speech models are now available for macOS, with Windows and Linux support coming soon.

The platform says that, thanks to Apple’s MLX framework, it achieved 35% faster speech generation than Gradium’s own implementation in tests on a MacBook Pro with M5 Max, while matching the word error rate of the reference implementation in Hugging Face Transformers.

Phonon supports five languages (English, French, German, Spanish, and Portuguese) with separate models for each language, as well as a multilingual model that supports all five.

Users can also choose from a variety of voices with different accents, including American and British English, depending on the model.

The new speech models are available now for Apple Silicon Macs running Ollama 0.40.11 or later. Users can get started by downloading Phonon directly through Ollama.

To listen to audio samples or learn more about Ollama’s new speech generation capabilities, including instructions and code examples for using the models through its API, follow this link.

title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World
snippet: Meta has launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI.
fullText:
Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI. The might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse.

The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android. The app, spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, lets you pick and grow a virtual pet, feed it, and play with it. 

We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.

Meta’s description of the app indicates that it doesn’t want the app to be a habit builder. The company’s page also says that the app is not a chatbot, and is flagged as suitable for users older than 18.

“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives. Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you. No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.

“Not a chatbot. Not an assistant. Not a productivity tool. It’s a pet, and a place. Stay two minutes or twenty — it’ll be happy either way.”

The app also doubles as a journal, letting users describe their day through voice or text. The pet listens to the user and writes up the note in its own voice as an entry with a doodle. The app also features mini-games that you can play over a few minutes, and can send you a weekly email based on what it learned about you.

Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers. 

Until now, the social media giant has released AI-centric apps like Pocket, which lets you vibe-code games, and Vibes, which let you quickly generate videos.

Besides virtual pets, some companies have also tried making hardware AI pets.

title: Bank of America kindly asks that you don’t share your banking password with your AI assistant
snippet: The banking giant reminds customers that "you're responsible for activity" resulting from your AI agents' access.
fullText:
2:44 PM PDT · October 27, 2026

											

			

Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent.

In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.”

You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular. Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account.

This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money. As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt, banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time.

A spokesperson for Bank of America confirmed the authenticity of the bank’s email that was posted to social media. But heed the bank’s warning, for if things go wrong, it’s on you. Account agreements at most banks hold customers responsible for anyone they give their log-in to. “If you do share your credentials,” its email reads, “keep in mind that you’re responsible for activity resulting from that access.”

(via Bryan Toporek)

title: INMO GO3 smart glasses pack a display and Gemini integration with clever camera privacy
snippet: There are two problems with smart glasses today. Most don’t deliver that futuristic display we all want to have, and the camera has become a serious point of friction. INMO GO3 solve both problems while also supporting Google’s Gemini and more. more…
fullText:
There are two problems with smart glasses today. Most don’t deliver that futuristic display we all want to have, and the camera has become a serious point of friction. INMO GO3 solve both problems while also supporting Google’s Gemini and more.

The promise of INMO GO3 is to deliver an AI-forward pair of smart glasses that help you stay connected and get things done, but without using your phone quite as much. It delivers on that through software, of course, but also the fact that it puts an actual display in front of your eyes. So, unlike most existing smart glasses, you’re able to interact with everything without interrupting a conversation or glancing at your phone. The MicroLED displays – one for each eye – are bright (up to 1,500 nits) and have a 30-degree field-of-view.

One of the core features is translation, with GO3 supporting real-time translation across 98 languages, and even supporting 13 languages fully offline. The glasses detect speech from the person in front of you and put a translation of that right in your eyeline, letting you get over the language barrier without putting your phone in the middle. Similarly, GO3 can take notes during meetings, and coming soon, it will also be able to present summaries directly through the glasses.

The display can also be used as a teleprompter, or to interact with an AI assistant. INMO’s AI assistant is powered by Google’s Gemini and OpenAI’s ChatGPT and can do things such as answer questions, recognize images taken by the camera, and take notes, among other functions. The display can also be used for turn-by-turn navigation to help you get around without using your phone.

	

Despite all the additional functionality here, INMO GO3 remain lightweight. The glasses weigh in at 58g, just a tiny bit heavier than Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses – the ones without a display. The 8mm temples also ensure these don’t stand out in a bad way – they just look like normal glasses!

One of the coolest features here is the battery. Smart glasses by their very nature are limited in terms of how long the battery can go, so INMO designed the battery to be interchangeable. When the first battery drains, simply swap out the power pack with a fresh one that’s on the charger and keep wearing the glasses. The included charging case can still top off the battery, but a replaceable cell gets you up and going faster.

As mentioned, there is a camera on board here, but one of the really thoughtful additions INMO offers is a privacy cover. This physical shade covers the camera lens, providing some visible confirmation that the camera is not in use.

INMO GO3 also gets some boosts from accessories such as a speaker that can be used alongside AI translation to respond to the other person in their language, but using an AI clone of your voice. There’s also a controller ring you can wear to interact with GO3’s software without touching the actual glasses. Finally, you can also add on a sunglasses cover to improve GO3’s usability outside, and there are prescription lens inserts too.

INMO GO3 is on sale now for just $509.

Most IT teams have a reasonable handle on what AI apps are installed across their Mac environment. Your device management vendor can show you what’s running; policies can block which apps shouldn’t be there; and vendors have been adding AI visibility features over the past year. The app layer is mostly solved, but the browser remains a concern depending on your environment.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been an Apple IT admin since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade WiFi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

The app layer is the easy part

When AI governance topic comes up, it’s usually about:

Which AI tools are installed? 

Which ones are approved? 

What data can they access? 

Those are all actual questions that IT teams should know, and if they don’t, then that is priority one. If an employee installs an unapproved AI coding tool or a local model inference engine, IT can detect it, flag it, and automatically remove it. That part of the problem is largely within reach for any organization running a managed Mac fleet.

The browser is where data actually leaks

Here’s the bigger issue for most IT teams: an employee opens Safari or Chrome, goes to ChatGPT or Claude, logs into their free personal account, and uploads a corporate document to ask the model a question about it. No app was installed, and nothing shows up in your app inventory report from your device management vendor. The action happens entirely inside a browser that IT typically has no visibility into at the web application layer, depending on your filtering setup.

Jamf is addressing this directly with browser AI governance coming in Q4 2026. The capability will let admins identify the use of personal AI accounts in Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and other browsers, and enforce policies at the point of action, including blocking actions. I am very interested to see this in action once it arrives.

The enterprise browser approach

A different answer to the same problem is the enterprise browser, and I think many orgs will consider this going forward. Island is the most prominent example in this space that I’ve seen. The idea is that instead of trying to bolt governance into an existing browser from the outside that’s not necessarily native, you give employees a managed browser that IT controls from the ground up. Every use case happens inside a container IT governs, including which web AI tools employees can access, whether they can paste corporate data into a prompt, and what can be downloaded or uploaded to it.

The tradeoff is there, though. Asking employees to switch their primary browser is a harder ask than deploying a policy through an extension, and on Mac specifically, Safari is deeply integrated in ways that make replacing it as their daily browser likely to meet pushback. Chrome runs into the same problem. Island is growing rapidly, though. They recently announced a $400 million Series F round at a $ 6.4 billion valuation, and I think their model might end up being the default for many enterprises.

Ultimately, the tools to manage this are either just arriving or still in development; the policy frameworks haven’t caught up with the coming technical capabilities, and use cases change quickly.

Wrap up

AI governance on the Mac is not just about managing which AI apps are installed. It’s much harder than that. The browser is where corporate data actually moves to personal AI accounts, and it’s the part of the stack that traditional Apple management tools were never designed to govern at the web application layer. I expect this market to evolve a lot in the coming years.

title: M6 MacBook Pro vs M5 MacBook Pro: What’s actually changed?
snippet: Today Apple unveiled a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip. It has the same design as before and many of the same features, so what’s actually changed? Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Today Apple unveiled a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip. It has the same design as before and many of the same features, so what’s actually changed? Here’s what’s new.

#1: M6 chip

Here’s a quick rundown of how the M6 chip compares to last year’s M5, per Apple:

M6 chip

12-core CPU with 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores 

12-core GPU

Dual 16-core Neural Engine 

Up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth

M5 chip

10-core CPU with 4 super cores and 6 efficiency cores

10-core GPU

16-core Neural Engine

153GB/s memory bandwidth

In real-world use, here are the gains Apple says to expect: “The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5.” 

Finally, here are some pro workflow examples that compare the M6 MacBook Pro to the M5:

Up to 1.3x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing

Up to 1.3x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender

Up to 1.2x faster image-processing performance in Affinity

Up to 1.3x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode

#2: N1 wireless chip

Apple’s N1 wireless chip that first debuted in the iPhone 17 is now included in the MacBook Pro too.

N1 gives the new MacBook Pro two main upgrades:

Wi-Fi 7 support, up from Wi-Fi 6E

Bluetooth 6, up from Bluetooth 5.3

Apple also says that N1 improves the performance and reliability of certain features such as AirDrop and Personal Hotspot.

M6 MacBook Pro vs M5 model: wrap-up

Surprisingly, that’s the end of the list for M6 MacBook Pro upgrades. The new model is solely a spec bump update, with two new chips and no other listed changes.

That said, the M6 MacBook Pro is still a fantastic computer for anyone who wants Apple’s latest chip with a great Liquid Retina XDR display and excellent battery life.

But if you’re interested in something more radically new, Apple’s redesigned MacBook Pro with high-end chips is expected to be unveiled tomorrow.

title: Apple memory supplier expects price increases through at least 2030
snippet: Key Apple memory supplier SK Hynix has warned that RAM and flash memory shortages are likely to last through at least 2030, keeping product prices high. Apple is believed to be one of 14 customers who have locked in priority orders, but the contract does not protect against price increases related to the balance of supply and demand … more…
fullText:
Key Apple memory supplier SK Hynix has warned that RAM and flash memory shortages are likely to last through at least 2030, keeping product prices high.

Apple is believed to be one of 14 customers who have locked in priority orders, but the contract does not protect against price increases related to the balance of supply and demand …

The company says that while AI continues to drive demand and growth, there is little that can be done in the short to medium term to increase supply.

Supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.

The Register reports that SK Hynix has long-term deals with 14 tech giants for priority orders, but these allow for market-based price increases.

14 big buyers […] will collectively buy more than half of its output during 2027 and 2028, and some of them want to extend those agreements. The Korean giant doesn’t mind that because the deals include “a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers”

Apple is used to being in the driving seat when it comes to negotiating with suppliers, but this is not the case where memory and flash storage is concerned. Here, the shortages mean that it will have been forced to agree to contracts that allow significant price hikes in order to obtain guaranteed supplies.

Nikkei Asia also reports that printed circuit boards may be the next component to experience constrained supply. Once a humble commodity item, advances in the technology has turned them into specialist tech, with more layers and higher bandwidth requirements. The report says “that complexity shrinks the supplier pool and extends lead times.”

Apple said back in June that the company was doing its best to mitigate the price increases, but it has so far been unable to do so.

Echo Time

Echo Time is a camera-free smart alarm clock powered by Alexa Plus, Amazon’s generative AI assistant. The device has hundreds of selectable clock faces and built-in sleep tracking sensors designed to monitor your rest and optimize wake-up times.

			

More from CNET

Here’s how it works: With the optional smart alarms feature, Alexa will detect when you’re in light sleep and wake you within 10 to 60 minutes of your scheduled alarm. It uses sensor technology called Omnisense to monitor room temperature, your presence, proximity and breathing. 

Echo Time received the National Sleep Foundation’s SleepMark, which is awarded to products that meet evidence-based sleep standards.

Echo Time is now available for $200 in graphite, glacier white and coral pink, with an adjustable stand sold separately for $40. Certain features will require Alexa Plus, which comes with a Prime membership ($15 a month or $139 a year). 

Customizable clock faces allow you to choose between analog designs, nature backdrops, seasonal themes or your favorite sports teams and characters.David Carnoy/CNET

Amazon Kids Echo Time

There’s also a version for kids, called Amazon Kids Echo Time, that lets them set alarms, ask questions, swap out clock faces and check the weather. A Sleep Studio feature offers curated bedtime content.

Parents can use the Amazon Parent Dashboard to control sleep schedules and more, as the Amazon Kids Echo Time is powered by Kids Plus, a subscription with parental controls and for content selected with kids in mind. 

Available in galactic grape and cosmic lime, the Amazon Kids Echo Time starts at $210, and a one-year Kids Plus subscription is included. After that, plans start at $8 a month. 

Echo Show 16

Echo Show is Amazon’s smart speaker and display. The new Echo Show 16 has a 16-inch high-definition screen, built-in Fire TV and screen styles that let you turn the Show 16 into a digital photo frame, a smart home dashboard to control all your Alexa devices or a family organizer to manage tasks, color-coded schedules and meal plans. 

When compared to the Echo Show 15, the latest model has 10% more viewing area, a frame that’s about 40% thinner, 20% more computing power, upgraded audio and a new wide-angle 13-megapixel camera with the widest field of view ever offered on an Echo Show. Now, there’s also night vision. 

Echo Show 16 comes with Alexa Plus, which is required for certain features and included in a Prime membership. 

With the Echo Show 16 Fire TV, you can stream content from Netflix, Disney Plus, YouTube, Prime Video, HBO Max and more.David Carnoy/CNET

It will ship later this year, but the Echo Show 16 is now available for preorder with $100 off. The standard display costs $500, while the anti-glare Nanomatte version is $570. A standard stand costs $70, while a flexible swivel-and-tilt stand costs $125. Both are sold separately.

Alexa Photo Frame

The Alexa Photo Frame works with Amazon Photos to automatically sync and display your photos on its 10-inch, anti-glare, high-definition touchscreen. 

It’s the first and only photo frame with Alexa built in, so you can ask Alexa to show your favorite photos based on when they were taken, their mood or who’s in them. You can also add voice notes to any photo. 

The Alexa Photo Frame is available in black, birch and walnut frames.David Carnoy/CNET

The Alexa Photo Frame starts at $200. It comes with 90 days of Alexa Plus. For Prime members, Amazon Photos offers unlimited photo storage.

Echo Studio with Home Camera

The new Echo Studio speaker uses Advanced Room Adaptation to automatically adapt sound to your space, while Adaptive Volume adjusts what’s playing based on where you are in the room.

It uses the built-in Home Camera to do so, giving Alexa visual intelligence and letting you operate Live View to see your home when you’re away. In the future, you’ll be able to pair the Echo Studio with Home Camera and a Fire TV device, allowing you to take video calls on a larger screen. No specific date for this integration has been announced.

All Echo devices have a dedicated button to turn off the microphones and cameras, and visual indicators let you know when an Echo device’s camera is streaming images or video to the cloud. For those who don’t want a camera, the standard Echo Studio is still available. 

The Echo Studio with Home Camera is only available in graphite, a dark gray. David Carnoy/CNET

Echo Studio with Home Camera is now available for $250. An optional stand is $40. The standard version is still available for $220. 

Echo Dot

The new sixth-generation Echo Dot speaker delivers crisper vocals and 50% more bass than the previous model. Upgraded on-device processing and a fourth microphone allow for faster, better conversations with Alexa Plus. 

For the first time, the Echo Dot also has a built-in smart home hub, so you can control compatible smart devices without a separate device. 

Amazon Kids Echo Dot offers the same features as the Echo Dot, plus a year of the Kids Plus subscription included. 

You can get the Echo Dot in graphite, glacier white, agave green and coral pink.David Carnoy/CNET

Echo Dot is now available for $100. Amazon Kids Echo Dot starts at $110.

Alexa Home Map

On compatible apps, Echo and Alexa devices and Fire TVs, Alexa Home Map will roll out as an interactive 3D map feature that shows both the inside and outside of your home. With a compatible Ring camera, you can see animations showing where people and cars are located. Through Ring’s Familiar Faces tool, an AI facial-recognition feature that has drawn privacy criticism, the display can identify specific recognized visitors by name.

Alexa Home Map also displays the locations of all other smart home devices, including Echo devices, Ring and Blink cameras, Fire TV, lights, locks and thermostats. 

From the interactive map, you can check security cameras, turn off lights and monitor device activity at a glance. Visual status cues appear directly on the layout, where smart lights reflect their current brightness and color, and active smart speakers display animated musical notes. 

To get started, add your address to Alexa Home Map, and it will automatically generate your home’s exterior. Using a compatible iPhone, walk through your house to map the interior. Then, manually add your devices’ locations on the map. 

The Alexa Home Map updates in real time to show you the weather, cars and people. Amazon

Later this year, Alexa Home Map will roll out in preview on its own iOS app, the Alexa and Ring apps, the Ember Artline Fire TV, new Alexa Tablets and larger Echo Show devices, including the Echo Show 16.

Certain features will require Alexa Plus, a Ring Pro subscription ($20 a month or $200 a year) or a Virtual Security Guard subscription ($99 a month) with compatible Ring cameras.

title: Kodiak lands first commercial deal to supply driverless trucks for public highways
snippet: The deal with DTL Transport puts it on a path to become an an asset-light tech supplier, rather than owner and operator.
fullText:
Kodiak AI will deliver 75 self-driving trucks to freight company DTL Transport starting in 2028. It’s the company’s first binding commercial deal for driverless big rigs that will run on public highways.

The contract, announced Wednesday, comes just ahead of Kodiak’s next big milestone: pulling human safety operators out of the cab to begin operating a driverless highway service in December. The company, which went public in September 2025, plans to launch that service by carrying goods for Ikea on Interstate 45 between Dallas and Houston.

DTL Transport, a California mid-market trucking company that hauls fresh produce and goods to grocery chains, plans to use the self-driving trucks on multiple interstate highway routes, starting with Dallas to El Paso, Texas, and Interstate 20 between Dallas and Atlanta. Kodiak has already conducted testing and operations on those two routes. 

“One of the things that we love about mid-market carriers (like DTL) is that they are able to move with fast execution speed, much more at the speed of a startup or a small company or a tech company like Kodiak, and that they just want to get stuff done,” Kodiak founder and CEO Don Burnette told TechCrunch in an exclusive interview. “It’s easier for them to integrate into their fleet because they’re not as large, and we think that this is a real turning point for the self-driving industry in general.”

The contract should give Kodiak a revenue boost and a positive benchmark. Its shares have fallen 87% from their opening-day price. It also puts Kodiak on a path to become an “asset-light” technology supplier, meaning it would sell its technology rather than own and run trucks itself — a goal it shares with competitor Aurora Innovation.

Today, Kodiak has a number of customers under a Trucking-as-a-Service (TaaS) model, including Charger USA, Roehl Transport, and Werner Enterprises. Under this business model, Kodiak owns and operates the self-driving trucks as a third-party carrier on behalf of other companies. It currently carries freight for these companies on a few routes in Texas. Kodiak generates revenue carrying freight daily for these companies on three active routes, but Burnette described these operations as still being in pilot stage.

Ultimately, Kodiak wants to move to a Driver-as-a-Service (DaaS) model, in which customers own and operate the trucks. Kodiak licenses its technology, charging customers by the mile for the duration of the contract. DTL is Kodiak’s first on-highway DaaS customer, a relationship that was forged during a pilot program last month in California. In that pilot, Kodiak autonomously hauled perishable goods for DTL about 225 miles along Interstate 5 and California State Route 99 between Fresno, California, and Los Angeles, with a human safety operator behind the wheel.

“You have to prove out the technology first using your own truck, show them that it works, show them that it’s safe, show them that it integrates,” Burnette said, describing the Trucking-as-a-Service model. “And then we want to be asset light. We don’t want to be in the business of running a trucking company.”

Atlas Energy Solutions has been a Driver-as-a-Service customer since 2024. Technically, Atlas was Kodiak’s first customer under a binding commercial contract, but its driverless trucks operate in off-road settings in West Texas’ remote Permian Basin. Atlas currently owns and operates 35 driverless trucks equipped with Kodiak’s self-driving system. Burnette said Kodiak is on track to have as many as 100 in service there by mid-2027.

Kodiak didn’t reveal the value of the deal with DTL Transport. However, its public 2025 investor presentation offers some clues about the contract’s potential value.

In that document, Kodiak forecast annual recurring revenue of $150,000 to $190,000 per truck. That forecast rests on several assumptions, including a per-mile licensing fee of about $0.97 (in line with current human driver costs per mile), annual mileage of about 225,000 miles a year per truck, and other factors.

Assuming those projections bear out, the deal with DTL Transport could generate at least about $11.2 million in annual recurring revenue once all 75 trucks are delivered.

		Kirsten Korosec is a reporter and editor who has covered the future of transportation from EVs and autonomous vehicles to urban air mobility and in-car tech for more than a decade. She is currently the transportation editor at TechCrunch and co-host of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast. She is also co-founder and co-host of the podcast, “The Autonocast.” She previously wrote for Fortune, The Verge, Bloomberg, MIT Technology Review and CBS Interactive.

title: Public Discord messages might start showing up in Google Search, unless users opt out
snippet: Discord announced today that Discoverable Server web pages will begin showing summaries and pulled content, which might show up in search engines. more…
fullText:
Discord announced today that Discoverable Server web pages will begin showing summaries and pulled content, which might show up in search engines.

Discord splits its servers into three different types: private, community, and discoverable. The latter is the most public version. No one needs an invite, and anyone can message, given that the admins of that server haven’t blocked you completely.

In a recent press release, Discord notes that all Discoverable Servers will get a Server Web Page. The page is essentially an overall summary of that server, so users can easily gauge whether they its something they want to join.

Discord says that discussion summaries will also appear on those server web pages, extracted from public channels. Any conversation that might be deemed noteworthy, whether by an AI model or moderator, could appear on that web page, and by extension, search engines like Google.

	

It sounds like Discord is hoping channels surface in Google’s AI Mode or other engines, like Reddit, when users search for certain topics. It’s not a bad idea, as message boards often contain answers to incredibly niche questions otherwise hard to find on the internet.

The release makes it clear that server admins can exclude certain channels and channel summaries, but doesn’t say the entire server can opt out. That seems to only be possible by switching server types.

Individual users can also opt out. Users can head to User Settings > Data and Privacy to control whether their public messages appear in the server web page.

Discord says these changes will take effect starting November 16. Admins and users wishing to opt out of having their public messages and channels included in web pages, and by extension, search results, will need to opt out before then.

title: Apple wins expanded access to evidence in OpenAI trade secrets lawsuit
snippet: Apple has scored another win in its trade secrets misappropriation lawsuit against two former employees, OpenAI, and io Products. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple has scored another win in its trade secrets misappropriation lawsuit against two former employees, OpenAI, and io Products. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Earlier this month, Judge Edward Davila granted some of Apple’s requests for expedited discovery in the lawsuit where the company accuses two former employees (Chang Liu and Tang Tan), as well as OpenAI and io Products, of trade secret misappropriation.

As we’ve been covering since July, Apple filed this lawsuit accusing the defendants of improperly accessing or using confidential information about its products and technologies to help advance OpenAI’s consumer hardware development efforts.

As part of the lawsuit, Apple asked Judge Davila to issue a preliminary injunction (aimed at preventing the defendants from further using its alleged trade secrets), as well as expedited discovery to obtain early access to internal documents, forensic evidence, and employee testimony.

In his decision partially granting Apple’s request for expedited discovery, Judge Davila gave the company early access to select internal documents, forensic evidence, and employee testimony.

However, he postponed ruling on several other requests, finding Apple’s definition of “Apple Originated Information” too broad.

Following the decision, Apple and the defendants agreed on a narrower definition of the term, which Judge Davila has now adopted (with modifications), allowing Apple to pursue additional discovery.

Today’s decision

In his new decision, Judge Davila granted several of Apple’s previously deferred requests, expanding the company’s access to records concerning its former employees’ handling of confidential information, their use of AI tools, and OpenAI’s recruitment and hardware development practices.

That includes:

Records of Liu’s use of ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, OpenClaw, and other AI tools, including on personal and corporate devices and accounts.

Details about devices, accounts, and messaging apps Liu and Tan allegedly used to access, store, or share confidential Apple information.

Details about any confidential Apple information that may have been deleted or destroyed, including when, how, why, and by whom

Testimony from OpenAI and io Products representatives about work involving Apple information related to batteries, power management, and metal finishing.

Testimony about OpenAI’s interviews involving Apple employees, including whether confidential Apple information was discussed or solicited.

Testimony about steps OpenAI took (or failed to take) to prevent unauthorized use or disclosure of Apple information.

That said, he also denied Apple’s requests for details about OpenAI’s own devices and accounts, its internal investigations, and any potential deletion of confidential Apple information.

He also denied two additional requests for corporate testimony, finding that they were “too broad at this stage and better suited for merits discovery,” meaning Apple can pursue them through the regular discovery process.

Under the new order, the defendants have up to 14 days to produce the requested records and respond to Apple’s questions.

title: Firefox’s AI-powered Smart Window gets form autofill and website monitoring
snippet: Mozilla today announced two new features for Smart Window, its opt-in AI-powered browsing experience in Firefox. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Mozilla today announced two new features for Smart Window, its opt-in AI-powered browsing experience in Firefox. Here are the details.

Smart Window adds two features

Nearly one year ago, Mozilla announced plans to introduce AI Window, an opt-in experience that would let Firefox users interact with an AI assistant while browsing, with features like summarizing content, comparing information across tabs, and answering questions without leaving the browser.

Since then, the feature has been renamed Smart Window, and it has gradually gained new capabilities.

A few months ago, for instance, Mozilla introduced AI-powered web search to Smart Window, alongside automatic tab grouping, duplicate tab detection, and the ability to search browsing history using natural language.

Today, the company announced two additional features rolling out to Smart Window beta users: AI-powered form filling and website monitoring.

As Mozilla explains, the AI-powered form-filling feature can draw context from other open tabs to suggest answers for web forms. This means it goes beyond traditional autofill, which typically handles basic information like names, addresses, and contact details, by generating responses based on information found on other currently open pages.

Here’s Mozilla:

For example, Smart Window could use information from your online portfolio or professional profile to fill in your work history, or draw on those details to draft an answer to a question like “Tell me about a time when…” Firefox’s regular autofill still handles saved information such as your name and address, which can be entered directly into forms without relying on AI models.

Mozilla notes that the feature relies on Google’s Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite model to analyze form fields and extract relevant information from selected tabs, meaning that information from those pages is shared with the AI model for processing.

The second feature rolling out today is website monitoring, which works similarly to Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature introduced with iOS 27 and macOS 27.

It lets users type /watch in the Smart Window chat to tell Firefox to monitor webpages for specific changes, such as price drops, product availability, or new job listings. Firefox then notifies users when those changes are detected.

Users can choose between daily and weekly checks, with up to 5 webpages per task, though monitoring runs only while Firefox is open.

Here’s Mozilla again:

When there’s a match, you’ll see an update through the Tasks button in the toolbar. With desktop notifications enabled, Firefox can also notify you directly; click the notification to open the watched pages. You can have up to 15 active tasks at a time, and you can edit, pause or delete tasks. Smart Window will automatically pause tasks after 60 days without a matching change. If 90 days pass without a change, it will stop checking altogether.

As with AI-powered form filling, the feature relies on an AI model to process information, although in this case Mozilla uses Qwen to identify changes that match what users are looking for.

Both new features are now available in the Smart Window beta for Firefox desktop, though they’re currently limited to English-language users in the US and Canada. Mozilla says they will “roll out to additional markets in the coming months.”

snippet: Astropad is out today with Workbench 1.4, the latest update to its remote desktop app for Mac. The release adds a built-in terminal, native iPhone Duo support, and a new way to transfer files between Macs. more…
fullText:
Astropad is out today with Workbench 1.4, the latest update to its remote desktop app for Mac. The release adds a built-in terminal, native iPhone Duo support, and a new way to transfer files between Macs.

Workbench first launched in April with a focus on accessing your Mac from an iPhone or iPad, including checking on AI agents while away from your desk. Version 1.3 arrived in August with faster streaming, a privacy curtain, picture-in-picture support, and tools for keeping unattended Macs accessible.

The big addition in Workbench 1.4 is the ability to switch between the remote desktop and terminal without reconnecting. A toolbar control lets users move between Screen and Terminal views. On Mac, the terminal opens in a separate window.

That means you can check logs, edit a script, or restart a process without opening a separate SSH app. Terminal sessions also keep running between connections, so you can start on an iPad and return later from an iPhone or another Mac.

Voice input works with the terminal as well, letting users dictate prompts and commands. For Mac-to-Mac connections, Workbench now supports dragging and dropping files during terminal sessions.

Astropad says the update also runs natively on iPhone Duo, with support for keeping an agent visible in one pane while using the rest of the phone.

Workbench remains free for 20 minutes of access per day. Unlimited access is currently priced at $14.99/month or $79.99/year. The app requires macOS 15 or later, iOS 26 or later, or iPadOS 26 or later.

title: Opera One now lets Mac users run Apple’s foundation model directly in the browser
snippet: Starting today, Opera One users can access a preview feature that lets them tap into local AI models through WebAI, a proposed web standard. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Starting today, Opera One users can access a preview feature that lets them tap into local AI models through WebAI, a proposed web standard. Here are the details.

WebAI

Opera announced today that its Opera One browser is the first of its browsers to offer built-in access to local AI models, with Opera GX and Opera Neon to follow.

The feature relies on the WebAI proposed web standard, which allows websites and browser extensions to access AI models running locally on the user’s device.

Here’s Opera:

WebAI is a proposed web standard, backed by companies such as Google and Microsoft, that lets websites and browser extensions use AI hosted through the browser. Opera’s implementation is model-agnostic and built around open models, offering users choice among AI providers. At launch, users can already tap into models from Google and Apple, including Google’s Gemma and, on Macs, Apple’s on-device foundation model, directly in Opera.

The company notes that WebAI can be used to generate text, classify content, and identify relationships between pieces of information, and adds that the feature is opt-in, with no subscription needed, and with users able to control which websites can access local AI models.

Here’s Opera again on some of the potential uses for local AI in the browser:

With local AI built into the browser, both users and developers can benefit from new capabilities. Local AI lets anyone build on top of free, open-weight AI models. Developers can add AI features without running AI infrastructure or paying for every request. Users don’t need AI subscriptions, the information the local AI handles stays on their own device, and they stay in control of the AI on their computer. For example, an extension could sort your tabs, flag clickbait or spot relevant job posts using a model on your laptop, with no account, no fee and no data sent to an AI service.

To help developers (and users) explore what’s possible with WebAI, Opera has released a collection of example extensions that you can find here.

HTML-in-Canvas

Additionally, Opera is launching HTML-in-Canvas today, which, as the company explains, “lets developers put real, interactive web pages inside 2D and 3D scenes.”

The feature allows developers to embed fully functional web pages into 2D and 3D environments, with interactive elements such as menus, buttons, and forms remaining usable even as they move around within a scene. Developers can build these experiences using familiar HTML and CSS.

Here’s Maciej Kocemba, Product Director at Opera GX:

“Honestly, this is a fun one […]. You can take a real web page and throw it into a 3D world, and everything still works: buttons, text, menus, all of it. We wanted users to get their hands on it early and see what they come up with.”

To demonstrate the possibilities, Opera has created two examples: Webpage Bulldozer, which turns elements of a web page into physical objects, and Gamer Room, a virtual 3D room featuring screens that display live web pages. Both demos work in Opera browsers without any additional setup, and you can check them out ⁠here.

title: Last Week’s Critical PHP Warning Was the Tip of the Web Vulnerability Iceberg
snippet: AI is finding new holes in the infrastructure of the internet. Is anyone around to patch them?
fullText:
For the past week, software engineers around the globe have been scrambling to update the backend of websites after a team using an OpenAI model discovered two major vulnerabilities in PHP, a critical piece of web software.

PHP, open-source scripting software that underpins as many as 70% of websites worldwide, can become outdated when website owners don’t update to newer versions of the software, making them vulnerable to attacks. Shortly after alerts were issued about the new vulnerabilities, new versions of PHP were issued, and site operators were urged to update. Some government websites went dark in Europe as these updates were applied, but for much of the web, it’s been left to individual website owners to apply the fixes.

But will they?

			

More from CNET

No law compels them to do so, although if a website suffers a data breach, the owner could be liable to customers or clients. And for web surfers, it’s not obvious what PHP version a site is running without running terminal commands or using an online PHP checker.

Given that some websites are no longer actively managed — I own a website that was latent and hadn’t had a PHP update or updates of its WordPress software in years, for instance — the PHP story has shown that the web’s aging architecture is proving to be insecure due to neglect and dwindling resources to keep it safe.

PHP security shortages

One of the most shocking revelations that has come out of the last week’s race to get websites updated and safe is that an organization tasked with making sure security flaws in PHP are addressed is itself on shaky ground.

Reuters reported that the PHP Foundation, a nonprofit formed in 2021 to work with researchers and cybersecurity companies to ensure a crisis like this wouldn’t happen, has only one full-time staff member and lacks the resources to expand.

The Foundation’s Executive Director Elizabeth Barron told Reuters that she’s the sole staff member and works with about 14 part-time contractors and unpaid board members. As AI-generated threats increase, there’s twice as much demand to change PHP code to address them as in the past. “Yet the number of contributors hasn’t doubled,” Barron said. While companies and governments rely on PHP, “It is clear PHP is severely underfunded,” she said.

A representative for PHP Foundation did not immediately return a request for comment.

Website operators may be unaware there’s a problem

Nearly all small businesses have some sort of web presence, whether it’s a social media account, a Google listing or a website they own. But small business owners, a survey from Network Solutions found, may not be addressing the PHP issue because they don’t know it affects them.

The report, based on a survey of 121 small business owners with their own websites, found 45% of them had never heard of PHP and 71% didn’t know if their websites use it. A large majority of 71% of these site owners hadn’t heard about the recent PHP flaws.

Rick Radinger, principal systems architect for Network Solutions Group, said that the survey showed awareness and knowledge gaps, but that in addition to not knowing about the current PHP problem, they may not think it’s their responsibility to act on a fix. “An owner might know about the warning but could assume their hosting provider will handle it,” Radinger said. “Others might need additional help but aren’t sure who to contact or next steps.”

Some of the mobilization about the PHP alerts included updates from large web infrastructure companies like Cloudflare and web hosts such as GoDaddy. In a blog post, Cloudflare said it deployed new web application firewall protections to detect and fend off attacks. GoDaddy made updates to its managed hosting and Windows hosting services that didn’t require website owners to take extra steps, but said that domain customers who manage their own sites or run virtual private servers may need to update PHP themselves.

In addition to its security updates, Cloudflare has also introduced a PHP Capture the Flag contest as part of its Bug Bounty Program on HackerOne. “We’ve put a deliberately vulnerable PHP installation behind our (firewall), and we’re inviting security researchers on HackerOne to try to bypass the protections and capture a flag,” Cloudflare said in its blog post. Cash prizes range from $100 to $10,000.

Frustration for web users

For those who don’t own a website, the PHP vulnerabilities aren’t something you can protect against by updating your passwords; it’s up to websites to stay updated to protect their visitors.

“For users, it is frustrating that they can’t fix this, as it is an issue with the site’s server, not the browser,” Radinger said. “Simply updating your browser doesn’t address the issue, and a site being up and running normally does not mean the site has been fixed.”

The usual advice applies more than ever: Be careful about clicking on unfamiliar website links, don’t share sensitive information with websites you don’t trust and be especially cautious about links that will download software to your device.

The PHP crisis is a good wake-up call about what’s happening to the World Wide Web as it approaches its fourth decade of operation. This latest security scramble is just one of the threats websites face (AI-generated breaches are a huge one). But many of the dangers to come may stem from aging digital architecture; PHP is just one of myriad tools websites use, including JavaScript, SQL databases, content management systems (like WordPress or Wix), and the software that the servers themselves run. If those aren’t regularly monitored, managed and updated across the web, you can expect a lot more vulnerabilities to emerge in the years to come.

title: OpenAI GPT models are coming to Google Antigravity ‘soon,’ Cloud ‘in the coming weeks’

fullText:
