title: Amazon’s New Alarm Clock ‘Knows’ if You’re in a Deep Sleep and Lets You Sleep Longer
snippet: The Amazon Echo Time, launched today, has a few wild features.
fullText:
Amazon is revamping its smart home devices, and it’s adding a new smart alarm clock to the lineup for the first time. Called the Amazon Echo Time, this alarm clock with unique AI sleep features is designed specifically for bedrooms — and bucking Big Tech’s “pervert tech” trend, it includes no cameras. It’s available now for $200 and starts shipping in December.

Amazon’s first clock is smart and customizable

The Echo Time looks like a regular Alexa speaker with one key difference: a 3.2-inch screen. You can customize the display to show an analog or digital clock, including themed variants from popular franchises, like Harry Potter, the DC Universe and Scooby-Doo. It’s one of many devices that Amazon dropped on Wednesday, including a revamped Echo Show, Echo Studio and a first-ever smart picture frame.

Customize the display to show an analog or digital clock and use popular themes including Harry Potter, the DC Universe and Scooby-Doo.David Carnoy/CNET

Inside, the device uses tech that adapts to your daily routines. For example, it can gradually get brighter in the morning to support your wake-up routine and reduce blue light at night to help you fall asleep. Those features are similar to other smart clocks, like the popular Hatch Sleep Clock. The clock also comes in two versions built specifically for kids, with controls parents can use, including Amazon’s Sleep Studio for bedtime-routine management.

			

More from CNET

A wild (opt-in) AI feature pushes the alarm back if you’re in a deep sleep

Like nearly every piece of tech these days, the Echo Time has optional AI features. If you don’t need to jump out of bed at a certain time, you can let the Echo Time handle your alarm. The clock then uses sensors that monitor room temperature and movement, including ultrasonic detectors for your breathing, to decide when to wake you. It works within a 60-minute window around your wake-up time, letting you get a deep sleep or waking you early if it detects your sleep is no longer “restful.”

If that sounds creepy or like something that will make you run late in the morning, don’t worry: It’s optional, and it requires an Alexa Plus subscription.

The new Echo Time clocks come in graphite, glacier white and coral pink for adults, with galactic grape and cosmic lime options for kids.David Carnoy/CNET

While this feature could be dangerous during workdays or before a flight, it sounds perfect for sleepy weekends when you’re trying to catch up on rest. 

There have never been more smart home tech options. Earlier this month, Apple revamped its options and introduced a brand-new device called the Home View. Apple’s new devices impressed CNET reviewers, particularly with their easy-to-use setup. But families that already use Amazon devices will likely want to stay within the same ecosystem.

fullText:
TikTok is launching an in-app restaurant guide in a challenge to other platforms like Yelp and even Google Maps.

The company on Wednesday announced the launch of Must Eat, a new section of the TikTok app built on 40 million posts, reviews, and comments about dining on the platform. The new feature uses videos and discussions of buzzy local businesses to create restaurant recommendation guides. Users can leave reviews of restaurants, call and make reservations, and search for nearby businesses on a map.

At a launch event this week, TikTok US CEO Adam Presser called Must Eat “the compilation of all of the conversation that’s happening on the TikTok platform across creators, restaurateurs, [and] individuals” who make videos or leave comments about local restaurants. Among the featured restaurants in New York are Golden Diner (home of very viral pancakes) and hard-to-reserve spots like Semma and Via Carota.

Must Eat falls somewhere between Yelp and more curated recommendations from publications like The Infatuation. Must Eat is divided into two category tabs: “everyday eats” and “elevated dining.” Users can sort and filter by rating, distance, cuisine type, and what’s currently open, and each page for a restaurant links to videos about the business posted to TikTok. Diners can also bookmark businesses to save them for later. The feature is initially available in a few select regions — New York City, Los Angeles, and the Bay Area. The company says restaurants can’t pay to be featured in the recommendation lists.

It’s not the first time TikTok has tried to bridge the gap for users between seeing a video about a place and actually visiting in person. Earlier this year, the company added the ability to book hotels and attractions through the app. That feature, TikTok Go, allowed content creators to tag and link to locations; Must Eat is an expansion of that earlier capability.

TikTok’s deeper move into the dining space is fitting, given the app’s profound impact on restaurants. Content creators have angled to become the food critics of the short-form video era, each with their own schtick or eccentricities. The popularity of food videos has even changed what restaurants put on the menu to begin with, like extra-long cheese pulls or dramatic presentations. In its press release announcing the launch of Must Eat, TikTok says 27 million US diners went to a restaurant, cafe, or shop for the first time thanks to the platform last year.

title: Chrome 156 for Googlebook rolling out with 14 updates across sites, shortcuts, more
snippet: Google is rolling out Chrome 156 for Googlebooks with a slew of improvements and bug fixes. This follows the last browser update two weeks ago. more…
fullText:
Google is rolling out Chrome 156 for Googlebooks with a slew of improvements and bug fixes. This follows the last browser update two weeks ago.

In terms of “New Features,” there’s “Hover Tooltips in the AI Mode Menu: Items in the address bar’s AI Mode menu now show tooltips on mouse hover.”

The remaining 13 updates today are classified as “Improvements.” On the keyboard shortcuts front:

Alt+Tab: Alt+Tab now switches windows on Fullscreen sites and apps when keyboard lock is on, as it does on ChromeOS, Mac and Windows. Users no longer need to hold Esc to exit before switching tabs.

Alt+Shift+Enter Shortcut: Alt+Shift+Enter now opens the typed query in a new background tab and keeps you on the current page.

Up/Down Arrows in Multi-Line Address Bar Text: Up/Down arrows now move the cursor between lines for easier editing when typed text wraps to multiple lines. Suggestions are hidden.

Specific website improvements include:

	

Google Docs: Enabled copying of large selections and tables in Google Docs. 

Facebook Live Video: Performance improvement of Facebook Live streams.

Stability fixes: Stability improvements were made across 1Password and other extensions, third party apps, and Chrome tab functionality.

Site Icons: Site and Google icons appear correctly when clicking into the address bar from a webpage or search results page. Stale site icons are removed when the URL bar is cleared.

There are some meaningful usability fixes:

Close Third-Party Sign-In Prompts: The close (X) button will close third-party sign-in prompts correctly. 

File Downloads: Added “Save As” dialog support to choose download save locations, and fixed a naming issue with duplicate file downloads so they open correctly in apps.

Right-Click on Incognito New Tab Page: Context menu now opens when right-clicking links on the Incognito new tab page.

Finally, the AI Mode updates continue with:

AI Mode Animation Timing: The AI Mode animation waits for the expansion to complete before playing and plays more consistently.

“Add to your search”: The menu for adding tabs and files to an AI Mode search now has an “Add to your search” header.

“View your AI Mode history”: The address bar now correctly displays “Ask anything” hint text and blinking cursor.

We’re seeing Chrome 156 for Googlebook OS widely rolling out via the Play Store today. It comes a week after the stable release started on desktop and mobile (not fully available for Android phones and tablets yet).

title: iOS 27.2 has two CarPlay improvements, here’s what’s new
snippet: iOS 27.2 arrived this week with new features for Messages, Apple TV, and more, plus two improvements for CarPlay. Here’s what’s new for CarPlay users. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 arrived this week with new features for Messages, Apple TV, and more, plus two improvements for CarPlay. Here’s what’s new for CarPlay users.

#1: Apple Podcasts adds sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing

Apple Podcasts in iOS 27.2 adds two new sections to the Home tab: ‘New Episodes’ and ‘Continue Playing.’

Essentially, Apple has rethought how the core ‘Up Next’ queue of its Podcasts app works.

Like you would expect, ‘New Episodes’ contains only the latest episodes from your favorite shows. But after you’ve started an episode, you’ll find it in the ‘Continue Playing’ row just below.

This overhaul to podcast management makes it easier to find the latest episodes of your shows and also pick up where you previously left off. I’m a big fan of the change.

#2: Siri AI upgrades

Siri AI introduces a variety of upgrades in iOS 27.2, including two that carry over to CarPlay as well.

Per Apple’s release notes:

Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week

Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List

It can take some adjustment to remember that Siri AI is available in the car just like on iPhone. But CarPlay is an especially useful platform for Apple’s more powerful assistant.

Bonus: Apple Music’s new app icon and design tweaks

It’s arguable whether this qualifies as an “improvement,” but it is a change worth mentioning. iOS 27.2 includes a new app icon for Apple Music, plus some minor design tweaks in the app.

These changes are related to the total rebrand Apple Music unveiled just last week.

For more new features in CarPlay that recently arrived in iOS 27, see our coverage here.

fullText:

Do you like to run? I’ve learned that I, apparently, do enjoy the hobby, but I hate the feeling of earbuds in my ears while I’m breathing heavily. That’s why I picked up a pair of CMF Clip Pro earbuds back in August: they’re clip-style earbuds with open-ear tips, so I don’t have to deal with the annoying pressure changes rubber-tipped earbuds can cause while working out. And now you can also enjoy them at the lowest price ever today with this CMF Clip Pro deal.

CMF Clip Pro at Amazon ̶$̶9̶9̶ now $69

I’m not sure why Nothing is discounting them on a random day in October, but I’m certainly not going to complain about a great pair of buds for under $70. CMF Clip Pro is normally $99, and they deliver good enough quality for the price, but this $69 sale makes them a no-brainer choice if you want to try out the latest clip-on earbud trend.

Because these hold on to your ears better than a typical set of buds, you can jump around, run, work out, or do basically anything else without having to worry about them falling off. I also appreciate the fact that their open-ear design lets me hear the world around me, which I think is vitally important while out on a run with traffic and who knows what else.

title: iOS 27.2 adds new Messages feature that’s already a favorite
snippet: iOS 27.2 launched this week with many new features for iPhone users, including a Messages addition that was previously announced for iOS 27 but later got pushed back: Suggestions. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 launched this week with many new features for iPhone users, including a Messages addition that was previously announced for iOS 27 but later got pushed back: Suggestions.

Messages ‘Suggestions’ return in iOS 27.2 after being pulled from iOS 27 beta

Throughout the iOS 27 beta this summer, one of my favorite AI features was a Messages addition that didn’t feel like AI at all: Suggestions.

Here’s what they do, per Apple:

Messages offers one-tap suggestions based on the context of users’ conversations, making it easier than ever to get things done, such as creating a reminder or a note. For example, if someone asks for photos, Messages can also help users find the right ones, recognizing keywords, locations, and people in their library to find the best options.

Suggestions appear as small, convenient action buttons beneath messages they’re relevant to.

As seen in the image below, if someone asks you to do something, you might see a suggestion to add to Reminders or Notes. Or if an event is mentioned, suggestions lets you easily add it to your calendar.

Suggestions worked well for me in the iOS 27 beta, but shortly before the public launch last month, Apple delayed the feature into a “future software update.”

Now in iOS 27.2, suggestions have officially returned, launching for all users. And one way they’ve changed might explain why they were pulled in the first place.

As I mentioned, suggestions performed as expected for me during the summer. But if I had one complaint, it was that they sometimes appeared when a message’s context didn’t merit them. At times I saw suggestions to add things to Notes, Reminders, or Calendar when there wasn’t a clear justification for these recommendations.

But in iOS 27.2, I’ve seen far fewer suggestions appearing in my Messages conversations. When I see them, it’s always obvious why they’re being offered. Clearly the feature benefited from a little extra fine tuning.

If you want even more control over the types of Suggestions that appear, you can manually configure categories under Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Messages ⇾ Suggested Actions.

title: My experience suggests Apple Glasses will only sell to existing eyeglasses wearers
snippet: No, I haven’t managed to get my hands on a prototype pair of Apple Glasses, but I now have experience of the rough equivalents of what we’re expecting from both a 1st- and 2nd-gen product. In both cases, I could definitely see attractions, and I would absolutely upgrade to smart glasses if I wore conventional eyeglasses. But as someone who doesn’t, I can’t see the technology persuading me to do so … more…
fullText:
No, I haven’t managed to get my hands on a prototype pair of Apple Glasses, but I now have experience of the rough equivalents of what we’re expecting from both a 1st- and 2nd-gen product.

In both cases, I could definitely see attractions, and I would absolutely upgrade to smart glasses if I wore conventional eyeglasses. But as someone who doesn’t, I can’t see the technology persuading me to do so …

1st-gen Apple Glasses

The first-gen Apple Glasses expected to launch next year will not have a display, only audio output. It will be something akin to Ray-Ban Meta glasses, only probably without the photo and video capabilities. The camera will only be used to power the Visual Intelligence features. 

Personally, I see this primarily as a stepping stone to a later, more sophisticated product with built-in displays. When I used the AI features in the Meta glasses, I found it very technologically impressive, but the novelty wore off very quickly and I didn’t find many practical uses.

The usefulness of this device will depend very much on the Apple Intelligence capabilities. I’ll certainly be interested to see whether Apple can make a convincing case for the first-gen device, but I find it very hard indeed to imagine the company would persuade non-eyeglass wearers to buy them.

2nd-gen Apple Glasses

The next generation, however, is expected to have a display. As a preview of this experience, I’ve been testing the Even Realities G2 smart glasses. 

I said when I first tried them that they are an extremely impressive piece of technology. They really do feel like something from the future, and friends who’ve tried them have said the same. 

At the time I began testing them, the UK was in the middle of a heat wave, so I was wearing sunglasses full time while outside anyway, and given how light these are, there was absolutely no downside to using these instead. 

Again, the AI features give great demo and feel very sci-fi, but I didn’t really find much practical use for them. Instead, I found the glasses great for three things:

Notifications

Navigation

Translation

My question at the time was what would happen when autumn arrived and I wouldn’t otherwise be wearing any kind of glasses? Would the benefits prove sufficient that I would wear them anyway?

For notifications, the answer is absolutely not. Yes, when I’m wearing them anyway, it’s extremely convenient to simply see a notification appear mid-air in front of me without having to look at a watch or pull out an iPhone. But I don’t allow many notifications, and unless you’re receiving a constant stream of important ones throughout your day, I can’t see anyone wearing smart glasses just for this. 

For navigation, my answer is yes … but the occasions on which this would be beneficial are relatively infrequent. The biggest benefit is when visiting an unfamiliar city, when it’s very welcome indeed, as it enables extremely easy navigation while still being able to enjoy all of the sights around you. In my hometown of London, it sometimes proved useful when walking or cycling to an unfamiliar place, but this was typically no more than two or three times a month. 

The single best application in my view is the translation feature. It’s absolutely fantastic to be able to be making eye contact with someone and to get an instant visual translation. I find this way better than all audio translation in my ears. Of course, unless they have a pair too, then the benefit is limited as they will need to be either listening or looking down at the phone when I’m speaking. But of course, that too is a rather infrequent need for most of us.

Who will buy them?

I think even if you don’t currently wear eyeglasses, if you travel frequently to a wide range of unfamiliar foreign cities, then smart glasses with a display make perfect sense. Between the navigation and translation features, I would view the purchase as a no-brainer. However, while that was once my life, back in my tech research days, that’s not the case today.

	

Maybe if I wore eyeglasses and could justify the cost for the gadget factor and a bit of convenience, then I might shrug and say, why not? If your prescription is stable and you’re going to be able to use them for a number of years, then perhaps even relatively mild benefits would sell them.

But I would say for most people who don’t currently wear eyeglasses, they would be a very tough sell. If you’re not constantly being bombarded with notifications, aren’t often navigating to unfamiliar places, and don’t frequently have the need to understand people speaking a language you don’t speak yourself, then smart glasses like this are just very impressive technology that will spend most of their time gathering dust in a drawer.

Of course, Apple may pull something out of the hat here, just as it did with the iPhone Duo. The company took a form factor that was cute but compromised and appears to have turned it into a must-have device for a significant number of people. Perhaps it will do the same with Apple Glasses. Right now, however, my view is that if you wear eyeglasses and can afford them, you’ll probably want the 2nd-gen. If you don’t, then I can’t currently, well, see it.

What’s your view? Do you think Apple will come up with a killer app for either 1st- or 2nd-gen glasses, or simply implement the technology so well that you’d be willing to wear a pair routinely? Or do you think they will only sell to those who already wear eyeglasses? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

title: Motorola’s flagship Signature 27 sounds quite expensive in retail leak
snippet: Motorola’s return to the proper flagship space is coming in the Signature 27, but early leaks suggest this new device, as well as the company’s wide foldable, won’t exactly be cheap. more…
fullText:
Motorola’s return to the proper flagship space is coming in the Signature 27, but early leaks suggest this new device, as well as the company’s wide foldable, won’t exactly be cheap.

GSMArena and “Android Treasure“ spotted retail listings in Europe that give us some idea of what Motorola’s upcoming releases will cost.

The Motorola Signature 27 is listed at €1,594.90 through a retailer website based out of Portugal. For comparison, the Galaxy S26 Ultra is sold for €1,299 in Portugal. The listing calls out some marketing points including the 50MP Sony Lytia L910 main sensor, 200MP telephoto camera, as well as a “unique cooling system uses thermal gel with diamond particles and a new 3D vapor chamber to maintain performance for longer.” It also mentions weight of “0.4kg” which seems… unlikely given that would make for a phone that weighs 400g. Perhaps that’s the shipping weight. There’s also mention of a 12GB/512GB configuration.

Circling back to the price, it’s unclear whether or not that’s strictly accurate, but it’s not exactly out of the question.

	

With Motorola Signature 27 packing top-tier specs including Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, it was always going to be pricey. And if €1,600~ is the final price, it could be a lot worse. As a reminder, Oppo Find X10 Pro Max recently made its debut in the EU for €1,800. 

The same retailer also lists the “Razr Flex,” Motorola’s wide foldable, at €1,510~. This one very much seems like a placeholder listing given there’s no imagery and a generic description compared to the Signature’s listing. The price also seems borderline impossible seeing as the Galaxy Z Fold 8 sells for over €2,200 in Portugal. 

What these listings do suggest is that Motorola is gearing up for launch on these new products pretty soon. 

What would you pay for Motorola Signature 27?

title: Amazon’s new Echo line is here: the 6 biggest updates

The Echo Show 16 features … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Amazon has just taken the wraps off a bunch of new devices as part of a string of fall announcements. Today’s news focuses largely on new Echo speakers, with a few new smart home gadgets sprinkled in.

Here’s a roundup of all of the updates Amazon revealed on Wednesday.

Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 has a 16-inch display in an anodized aluminum frame that the company says is nearly 40 percent thinner than its predecessor. There’s a new Nanomatte display option to reduce glare, along with an audio architecture with micro woofers and two tweeters for clearer audio.

The Echo Show 16 features a wide-angle 13-megapixel camera, which Amazon says offers the “widest field of view” on an Echo Show device so far. It has 20 percent more computing power and an upgraded Omnisense fusion platform, allowing Alexa to turn up the heat when the room is too cold or turn on a light when you enter the room.

The Echo Show 16 is available for preorder today and costs $499.99, with the Nanomatte option priced at $569.99.

Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

Amazon is launching a new digital photo frame with a semi-matte, 10-inch touchscreen. The device syncs with Amazon Photos, allowing Alexa Plus to automatically pull up pictures based on who’s in it, when it was taken, and sentiment. You can also choose people you want to feature in your frame, as well as ask the device to show you specific pictures.

The Alexa Photo Frame costs $199.99 with a black frame or $229 for the birch and walnut frames.

Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

Amazon is rolling out an upgraded Echo Dot with a built-in smart home hub that can control devices around your home without a separate hub. Like the Echo Show 16, the Echo Dot also has the company’s Omnisense fusion platform to detect room temperature and presence. It has Amazon’s custom AZ3 chip as well, along with four microphones, a new full-range driver for 50 percent more bass than the previous generation, and a built-in Eero Wi-Fi extender. You can buy the Echo Dot today in black, white, green, and pink for $99.99.

Photo: Owen Grove / The Verge

Amazon built a camera into the Echo Studio. With this update, you can tap into a livestream of the room while you’re away from home, or ask Alexa questions about something in front of the camera. As an example, Amazon says you can hold up a board game to ask about the rules, or show it a box of cereal to order a different flavor. The Echo Studio with Home Camera will soon connect with compatible Fire TVs, too, giving you the ability to hold video calls on a larger screen.

The Echo Studio with Home Camera is available in black for $249.99, while its optional stand costs $39.99.

Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

Amazon has revealed the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock with a circular, 3.2-inch touchscreen that you can customize with different clockfaces and layouts.

The Echo Time offers an optional smart alarm feature that can wake you up when you’re in a lighter sleep — 10 to 60 minutes before your alarm — rather than at the exact time you want to wake up. It uses Amazon’s Omnisense technology to determine when to wake you up based on temperature and presence. The display also adjusts throughout the day, gradually brightening in the morning before dimming at night.

The Echo Time is available today for $199.99 in black, white, and pink, while a Kids Echo Time starts at $209.99. There’s also an adjustable stand available for $39.99.

Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

A new Alexa Home Map feature creates an interactive 3D map of the inside and outside of your home. It displays your Echo devices, Ring and Blink cameras, Fire TV, lights, locks, thermostats, and other smart home devices, which you can control directly through the map.

Amazon says you can create a map by entering your home address, scanning each room with a compatible iPhone, and then placing each smart home device. You can access your map in the Ring app, too, where you can view live animations of people and cars outside your home.

Alexa Home Map is rolling out in preview later this year on iOS in the Alexa Home Map, Alexa, and Ring apps. It’s also coming to larger Echo Show devices, the Ember Artline Fire TV, and new Alexa Tablets.

title: Major Even Realities G2 smart glasses update adds Conversate ‘Pro Mode,’ Knowledge Base
snippet: Even Realities today announced that a new software version will be rolling out to the G2 smart glasses, complete with a personal knowledge base that, thankfully, only remembers what you tell it. more…
fullText:
Even Realities today announced that a new software version will be rolling out to the G2 smart glasses, complete with a personal knowledge base that, thankfully, only remembers what you tell it.

When the G2 smart glasses launched, Even Realities packed them with features aimed at professionals, as well as tech geeks who appreciate retro mixing with the modern. But features like Conversate can be valuable to anyone in the right situation.

Even Realities says Conversate is getting an overhauled “Pro Mode” that pulls data from something it’s calling Knowledge Base – a feature that remembers the information and data you select. These feature refreshes are included in the Even Realities G2 version 2.4.0 update, which also upgrades the company’s AI interface to Even AI 2.0.

In order, it works like this:

	

Files and audio recorded in Conversate mode on the Even Realities G2 glasses, along with any manually uploaded files, sync to a secure Google Cloud Platform server in the EU.

Knowledge Base updates your information to disseminate.

Even AI 2.0 and active Conversate sessions pull context from the Knowledge Base.

Even Realities allows users to select up to 10 Conversate records to upload to that context tree during the initial setup. More can be added as they’re recorded. It also seems that new Conversate sessions need to be selected for upload and won’t be added to that database automatically, unless the user toggles automated uploads on.

Whatever data is there, Conversate Pro Mode will surface during relevant sessions. For instance, if you’re a sports journalist and have a backlog of recorded meetings in Conversate, new instances will provide context based on what you already know. It’s a more trustworthy approach than letting an AI model surface information it thinks is relevant. Even AI won’t stop doing that, but the Knowledge Base might be a more palatable source for some.

The biggest part of this update comes down to Even AI 2.0. Even Realities says it’s a “major upgrade” to how users interact with the G2 glasses as a whole. In reality, it comes down to quality-of-life changes that should make the smart glasses easier to use.

The G2 glasses are now able to activate Even AI with the touch sensor. When you hold it down, the recording starts, but stops when you release. And instead of requiring a new wake word for a follow-up, users can enable multi-turn conversations. Opening Even Hubs apps and changing certain settings right from the AI chat are supported, too.

Even Realities says Knowledge Base and Conversate Pro Mode will both launch today in beta. Because it’s still an early feature, it will be limited for users based on a monthly usage allowance. There’s no mention of pricing after beta in Even Realities’ press release.

Oh, and there’s a new tortoiseshell color option.

The legal battle between Oura, maker of the Oura Ring, and Ultrahuman, maker of the Ultrahuman Ring Pro, continues. On Friday, Oura announced in a blog post that it filed a new patent infringement lawsuit against Ultrahuman in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Texas. More from CNET

Oura’s smart ring legal battles

Oura sued Ultrahuman in Texas in 2023 for patent infringement over the company’s ring, then the Ring Air. In March 2024, Oura filed a patent infringement complaint with the US International Trade Commission against Ultrahuman, RingConn and Circular. Ten months later, the company filed another ITC complaint targeting Samsung’s Galaxy Ring, the Reebok Smart Ring, Zepp Health’s Amazfit Helio Ring, and Nexxbase’s Luna Ring.

This comes after Samsung preemptively sued Oura in May 2024 to prevent Oura from suing Samsung over patent infringement. As of July, the legal battle continues with a split outcome. 

In August 2025, the ITC ruled against Ultrahuman and RingConn for patent infringement. While Oura, RingConn and Circular reached settlements and patent license agreements, Ultrahuman’s Ring Air was banned in the US. 

In the meantime, Ultrahuman began working on its Ring Pro, unveiling the device and launching global sales in February while awaiting US Customs and Border Protection clearance. That approval came the following month.

However, Oura said that the previous US Customs clearance didn’t cover the two patents in its latest filing. One of those design patents was issued only two days before Oura’s filing. 

The Oura Ring 5 is the company’s latest model.Oura

Ultrahuman’s response

Ultrahuman remains confident in its Ring Pro and the innovation behind it, an Ultrahuman spokesperson told CNET in an email. As the court hasn’t yet ruled on Oura’s latest complaint, the company will continue to manufacture and sell the Ring Pro. 

“We will address Oura’s newly asserted claims through the appropriate legal process and will defend our position vigorously,” the spokesperson said. “Competition and intellectual property disputes are a natural part of building an important new technology category. They do not change our ambition or our pace.”

Oura’s response

“Ultrahuman has a history of copying Oura’s innovations, as demonstrated by the 2025 ITC ruling against the company,” an Oura spokesperson told CNET in an email. “Ultrahuman introduced a redesigned ring but failed to address continued infringement of Oura’s patents, seeking instead to capitalize on our innovation and the market leadership we have built.”

Oura also plans to vigorously defend the investment and ingenuity behind its products.

title: Apple unveils all-new iPad mini: OLED, thinner design, more
snippet: Apple has officially unveiled a new iPad mini. The company calls it the “biggest update ever” for the iPad mini, adding an OLED display and a thinner, lighter design. The new iPad mini is powered by the A20 Pro chip. Here’s everything you need to know. more…
fullText:
Apple has officially unveiled a new iPad mini. The company calls it the “biggest update ever” for the iPad mini, adding an OLED display and a thinner, lighter design. The new iPad mini is powered by the A20 Pro chip. 

Here’s everything you need to know. 

New iPad mini: Everything you need to know

Apple says the new iPad mini is even thinner than before, measuring 5.4 mm thick. For comparison, the previous-generation measured 6.3 mm thick. It weighs 255 grams, down from the 297 grams of the previous model. The new design is also IP67 rated for water and dust resistance. 

The new iPad mini also features an 8.5-inch OLED display, slightly larger than the previous 8.3-inch iPad mini display. Apple says this is due to 24% thinner bezels. The display reaches a peak brightness of 1200 nits. 

The press release and tech specs page for the new iPad mini don’t mention 120Hz or ProMotion support, so it appears to have a 60Hz refresh rate display. 

For performance, the new iPad mini is powered by the A20 Pro chip. However, there’s an interesting split between storage tiers. Here are the specs of the A20 Pro chip in the 128GB and 256GB models: 

5-core CPU with 2 super cores and 3 efficiency cores

7-core GPU

Neural Accelerators

Hardware-accelerated ray tracing

16-core Neural Engine

And here are the specs of the A20 Pro chip in the 512GB iPad mini configuration: 

6-core CPU with 2 super cores and 4 efficiency cores

7-core GPU

Neural Accelerators

Hardware-accelerated ray tracing

Dual 16-core Neural Engine

Apple touts that the new iPad mini has an “Acoustic Display.” Here’s how the company explains this technology: 

The new iPad mini features an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs. The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating.

The iPad mini’s 12MP Center Stage front camera is now located along the landscape edge. There’s also a 12MP Wide back camera with support for Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 frames per second. 

More specs: 

Apple’s N1 networking chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread

Cellular models feature Apple’s C2 cellular modem

Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro support

New iPad mini release date and price

The new iPad mini will be available for pre-order starting Wednesday, October 28, with the first orders arriving Friday, November 6. Pricing starts at $699 for 128GB of storage. It’s available in midnight and starlight colors. 

The 256GB and 512GB models are available with a nano-texture glass option as an additional $100 upgrade.

snippet: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 has the same form factor as Apple’s new iPhone Duo, but it’s in stock, discounted, and doesn’t have any cracking display issue at the moment. more…
fullText:
Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 has the same form factor as Apple’s new iPhone Duo, but it’s in stock, discounted, and doesn’t have any cracking display issue at the moment.

Apple’s first foldable is turning heads right now as many are considering buying a foldable for the first time. And rightly so. The iPhone Duo has a compact form factor, useful inner display, and good attention to detail in its software, and early reviews largely praise the device.

iPhone Duo review roundup: The same problems Android foldables face, but with Apple’s polish

But, now that it’s actually starting to ship, some customers have found that the inner display is facing a problem. While Apple hasn’t confirmed any major issues, it seems that there’s a hinge component that’s causing problems and, ultimately, causing the inner display to “crack” with green lines stemming from the center of the screen.

iPhone Duo displays are breaking, and you’re not folding it wrong

Not fun! 

	

Meanwhile, Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 shares the iPhone Duo’s same form factor (but thinner and way lighter), has excellent software, and was an absolute pleasure to use when we reviewed it earlier this year, all while display issues like this have not been reported in any capacity. 

And it’s just $1,699 right now.

Where the iPhone Duo starts at $2,000, Samsung has been discounting its popular foldable by $200 or more as of late. So, if you’ve been looking to buy a foldable for the first time, it’s at least worth a look.

title: From 8VC to Benchmark, here’s what’s hiding in October SEC filings
snippet: A whole crop of venture capital firms are raising significant new funds.
fullText:
October was a big month for venture funds, per SEC filings. The filings show that established names are currently commanding top dollar from LPs, especially with a specialized focus. Here are some of the most notable ones we found that haven’t been meaningfully announced or have seen important updates.

For one, Trust Ventures filed Monday to raise a $400 million Fund V. The Austin-based firm was founded in 2017 by Salen Churi to back founders building in highly regulated industries. Koch Disruptive Technologies notably backed the firm’s debut fund back in 2018. It previously sought to raise a $225 million Fund IV in 2023, though it’s unclear if or when that fund closed. Deep tech fund Interlagos Capital is also raising a $400 million Fund II. 

Elsewhere, Victor Lazarte and Kris Fredrickson, two former Benchmark VCs, have raised $1.252 billion for their debut AI fund called Diffusion ONE. Forbes previously reported back in May that the two had teamed up (after raising smaller funds of their own) to launch this fund with a target of $800 million, meaning it’s far surpassed that original target. The firm has already cut big checks since its debut, including co-leading Harvey’s $550 million Series H with Lightspeed Ventures and taking part in Etched’s $300 million Series C, announced in July. 

Speaking of Benchmark, the firm filed what looks like four new partner-only funds, called Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund T1, Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund 2, Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund 2-A, and Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund T1-A, seeking to raise $220 million, $132 million, $4.5 million, and $7.5 million, respectively. Jack Altman, who recently left his own firm to join Benchmark, is listed in each filing. 

Meanwhile, Joe Lonsdale’s 8VC also seems to be seeking to raise new vehicles — including a $400 million fund called 8VC DSS III; a $30.35 million fund called 8VC COSC; a $20.35 million 8VC BRSC fund; and a fund called 8VC AI Fund XI, which has already raised $13.5 million, including from 8VC itself. This follows the July news that 8VC raised $1.5 billion for Fund VII.

Earlier this month, Notable Capital, backers of companies like Anthropic, Airbnb, and Square, filed to raise a fifth fund, while Neil Mehta’s Greenoaks, which co-led Anthropic’s $65 billion Series H, filed to raise a fund called Greenoaks 7. The timing is good as Anthropic just took another major step in its efforts to go public, meaning the firms are already prepared to market themselves based on possible handsome returns. According to PitchBook, Greenoaks has also backed companies like Ramp and Anthropic.

Industry Ventures, meanwhile, has raised at least $1.7 billion for its secondaries fund, which opened in late July. The size of the vehicle shows how important that market has become, as appetite grows to buy into hot exiting private companies. One family office advisor told TechCrunch last month about how popular the secondaries market has become, while Emily Zheng, a senior VC analyst at PitchBook, said that stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI are some of the “most contested real estate in venture.”

Dominic-Madori Davis is a senior venture capital and startup reporter at TechCrunch. She is based in New York City.

title: OnePlus rolling out ColorOS to OnePlus 13, others as Android 17 update expands
snippet: OnePlus 13 is the latest OnePlus device to ditch OxygenOS for ColorOS as the brand’s Android 17 update rolls out more broadly. more…
fullText:
OnePlus 13 is the latest OnePlus device to ditch OxygenOS for ColorOS as the brand’s Android 17 update rolls out more broadly.

When OnePlus shut down in global markets earlier this year, it was announced that OxygenOS would go away in favor of ColorOS, with supported devices all moving over to Oppo’s Android skin going forward. The transition started last week, ahead of schedule, on the OnePlus 15, and is now expanding to more devices.

The most notable device in this latest batch is the OnePlus 13, the brand’s prior flagship and perhaps one of its most beloved devices in recent memory. Owners can expect their devices to be updated to ColorOS 17 starting in India, with other regions to follow in the coming weeks.

OnePlus is currently rolling out ColorOS 17 updates for the following devices:

	

OnePlus 15R

OnePlus 13

OnePlus 13R

OnePlus 13s

That’s in addition to the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4 last week, and almost everything is still limited to India for the time being. The only rollout that’s gone global thus far is the update for OnePlus Pad 4.

More on OnePlus:

I love the idea of adding some tracking capabilities with AirTag 2, but AirPods Pro 3 are still the most useful and actively functional add-on there is and you can still score them at $50 off via Amazon.

As we kick off a new work week, at just over two weeks from release, Amazon’s pre-order discount is still live on the new next-generation Apple TV 4K. While delivery times have been delayed into late November and December at this point, you can still lock in the early deal. 

Amazon still has the new Apple TV 4K sitting down at $289.99 shipped. This, as we have mentioned previously, certainly isn’t a giant deal, but it is the lowest price you’ll find out there. 

Delivery times have slipped just about everywhere at this point, and in most locations, so you might as well try your hand at Amazon where the price is a touch lower if you’re still looking to secure one. That said, Walmart has also dropped the price down to the same rate ahead of the November 13 release date and it might also be worth checking the delivery time you can get in your area over there as well. 

Apple TV 4K $289 (Reg. $299) | Amazon

Apple TV 4K $289 (Reg. $299) | Walmart

Walmart still seems to be suggesting it is getting them out on release day in some locations, but, like Amazon, you might actually have to place the order before getting an accurate estimate.

There’s also NFC support on this model through Baseus’ PowerSense system, similar to what we first saw on the PicoGo Air AM71. title: Samsung Galaxy Buds On Are the Premium Clip-On Earbuds You Didn’t Know You Were Waiting For
snippet: Samsung’s $229 clip-on open earbuds are primed to take on models from Bose, Sony and Shokz.
fullText:
Clip-on open earbuds are all the rage, and Samsung is the latest major brand to add clip-ons to its line of Galaxy earbuds with its new Galaxy Buds On. The style has grown so rapidly that it’s hard to believe Samsung didn’t already have a pair, but here we are. Available in black at launch, the Buds On list for $229 and ship in early November.

The Galaxy Buds On look like a lot of other clip-on buds already on the market. But at $230, they’re definitely one of the more premium-priced offerings. Though I haven’t tried them yet, I suspect they’ll offer strong performance for the category and be comparable to Bose’s new Sport Open Earbuds ($200), Sony’s LinkBuds Clip ($230) and Shokz’s Open Dots 2 ($200).

They have 11.3-millimeter drivers with dual woofers (TwinBoost Speaker, Samsung calls the drivers) to increase bass performance, which can often be suboptimal with open earbuds. Additionally, they’re equipped with three microphones along with a Voice Pickup Unit and AI algorithms (Intelligent Clear Call) that help eliminate background noise while homing in on your voice during calls.

			

More from CNET

This type of earbuds tends to fit quite comfortably and securely, and they’re an appealing choice for runners and bikers who want to hear the outside world for safety reasons. They have an IP54 rating, which means they’re splashproof and dust-resistant, and according to Samsung, “Computational modeling helped optimize speaker and battery geometry to create a low-pressure fit around the ear, while refining the stiffness and shape of the band for a secure, comfortable fit.”

Weighing 6.7 grams per earbud, the Galaxy Buds On have tap controls and support for head gestures. Samsung lists their battery life rating at up to 9.5 hours of music playback on a single charge — and up to 38 hours in total with the charging case, which features wireless charging.

The charging case appears to be very similar to other Galaxy earbuds charging cases.Samsung

With open earbuds like these that have drivers that sit over your ear canals without covering them, sound leakage can be an issue when you play your music loudly in quiet environments. These buds don’t have active noise canceling, but they are equipped with Samsung’s Audio Leakage Reduction technology that “reduces escaping sound before it travels outward by projecting reversed sound waves from the rear of the speaker, keeping audio more private to the listener.”

It’s also worth noting that the Galaxy Buds On are powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon S7 Gen 1 Sound Platform, which Samsung says facilitates extended playback periods at elevated volume levels with the help of a high-efficiency class-D amplifier “intricately designed to optimize power consumption.”

Samsung

If you have a Google Gemini account, you get always-on access to Gemini just by saying, “Hey Google, let’s talk live. Also, there’s a Quick Voice Memo feature that you can access by long-pressing on the earbuds and simply speaking (and thanks to Bixby, Samsung says, users can search recordings hands-free).

While the earbuds can be used with iPhones and other Apple devices, as their name implies, the Galaxy Buds On work best with Samsung Galaxy devices, with easy pairing and access to controls and EQ settings through a shortcut in Samsung’s Quick Panel. There’s also automatic audio switching between any Galaxy devices you own, though multipoint Bluetooth support is missing for owners of non-Samsung Galaxy devices. Android users can install Samsung’s Wearable app for customization options and firmware updates, but there’s no app support for Apple users (Samsung’s Galaxy Buds app for iOS only supports a few older legacy Samsung buds).

I’ll have a full review of the Galaxy Buds On in the coming days and will compare them to the aforementioned buds along with Bose’s Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen), which earned a CNET Editors’ Choice award for having the best sound in the category, though they’re $300 price makes them even more expensive than the Galaxy Buds On. The Anker AeroClip 2 currently have the best voice-calling performance for clip-on earbuds, so we’ll see how these Samsung clip-ons stack up against those Anker buds for calls.

by  Stevie Bonifield

Oct 28, 2026, 2:17 PM UTC

Image: Virgin Galactic

Stevie Bonifield

 

is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Virgin Galactic’s new spaceship is here, dubbed “Apeiron” by popular vote from a public poll. Apeiron is the first of the company’s new Delta-class spacecraft, but it isn’t slated to launch for nearly another year. Earlier this week, Virgin Galactic announced another delay in its launch timeline:

The lead Spaceship’s first commercial spaceflight is now expected in early Q2 2027, and the second Spaceship is expected to begin commercial spaceflight operations in late Q2/early Q3 2027. The updated timeline reflects additional time for completing avionics software integration and validation, which uses an exhaustive testing process. That testing will conclude at Spaceport America as the lead Spaceship is readied for its flight test series.

Virgin Galactic had previously delayed its next commercial spaceflight to February 2027, rather than late 2026. It’s now been over two years since Virgin Galactic’s last commercial spaceflight in June 2024, when it retired its VSS Unity spacecraft. Apeiron is leaving Virgin Galactic’s Mesa, Arizona Spaceship Factory on Wednesday onboard a captive-carry flight with its Eve launch vehicle, heading to Spaceport America in New Mexico, where Virgin Galactic says its “engineering team plans to complete avionics software validation before beginning flight tests.”

title: Instagram takes on YouTube with new 90-minute horizontal video format
snippet: According to The Hollywood Reporter, Instagram today began testing a new long-form horizontal video format with select creators in the U.S. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
According to The Hollywood Reporter, Instagram today began testing a new long-form horizontal video format with select creators in the U.S. Here are the details.

Instagram doubles down on long-form horizontal video

Every now and again, Instagram tries to go after YouTube with a new product. IGTV, for instance, was one of the social network’s attempts at competing in the long-form video space.

However, IGTV never really took off, and Instagram eventually phased it out as it shifted its focus to Reels.

Today, as reported by THR, Instagram kicked off a new attempt to compete with YouTube with Features, a new format that supports horizontal videos up to 90 minutes long.

Aimed at podcasters and other long-form creators, the feature has already been tested in Brazil and is now expanding to select creators in the U.S. It also lets them link shorter Reels to their full-length videos.

From THR:

Starting Monday, Instagram will be launching a test of horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes with select creators in the U.S. The product, called Features, is aimed at podcasters, comedians and other longform creators, with the ability to refer viewers to the full video from the shortform reels on the platform, which are typically around three minutes or less.

The move comes at a time when social media feeds and recommendations are increasingly filled with short clips from stand-up comedy performances and video podcasts, giving users snippets of much longer shows and episodes.

With Features, Instagram seems to be looking to capitalize on that trend, turning those clips into a gateway to full-length episodes.

According to THR, which spoke with Instagram VP of Product Tessa Lyons, the full-length videos will also be recommended to users on the Explore page and in other parts of the app.

Lyons told THR that users will be able to tap on a podcast clip in Reels to continue watching or jump straight to the full episode, without leaving Instagram.

Here’s Lyons elaborating on how Instagram plans to help creators monetize their long-form videos:

“For established creators who already have those relationships, they can bring that content with those placements and that branded content. And we also think that there’s a big opportunity for us to help creators who don’t yet have that infrastructure and that business behind them.”

THR notes that the move is part of the entertainment industry’s broader push into video podcasts, with companies like Netflix and Disney also bringing creator content to their platforms to compete with YouTube.

Instagram, meanwhile, has also expanded its Instagram for TV app to Apple TV in the U.S., and Features is now expected to play a role in the company’s broader push to leverage podcasts and other long-form videos to keep viewers engaged across devices.

title: The data center boom has an upside: innovation for the US grid
snippet: As the AI boom stresses the existing power grid, all sorts of new opportunities for grid modernization are also emerging as a result, industry insiders say.
fullText:
The AI boom has led to a gargantuan surge in energy demand across the country. Critics say this upswell in connections is enacting a stress test on America’s aging grid infrastructure. Worries abound that, in the short term, the energy crunch could lead to surging electrical bills and, in the long term, may eventually lead to outages or other technical problems.

At TechCrunch Disrupt earlier this month, industry insiders tempered much of this criticism with optimism about how the flood of new energy connections could actually be opening the door for grid modernization. Apoorv Bhargava, founder and CEO of WeaveGrid, Tim Heidel, CEO of Veir, and Kristin Eberhard, VP of policy at Rewiring America, said that though the grid faces new challenges, there are also plenty of new opportunities as well.

“It’s a very different electric grid, right?” said Bhargava. “We’re dealing with a ton of new variables, including renewable energy. We’re dealing with a ton of new load in the form of electric vehicles and data centers and heat pumps, and the ability to manage and orchestrate is fundamentally what utilities are now grappling with.” 

While all of those new connections are driving an ever larger amount of stress to the grid, Bhargava’s company hopes to provide the kind of load orchestration and management that helps utilities maximize the potential of the current system. WeaveGrid’s software can help organizations efficiently deploy energy while also optimizing connections to reduce utility payers’ bills, the founder said.

Heidel, on the other hand, runs a company that is working to build out and expand the physical infrastructure of the grid, while also making it run much more efficiently. Veir sells superconductive power lines that promise to transfer energy at a much more efficient rate than traditional ones. Veir’s cables can carry power five times farther than traditional cables while also requiring 20 times less space, the company has said. Earlier this month the startup raised $110 million in a Series C funding round.

“The scale of the investment in AI infrastructure is driving a tremendous amount of innovation,” said Heidel. “There’s a ton of new technologies that are coming off the shelves and starting to get to scale that, pulled together, can actually really make sure that data centers are the best community neighbors and citizens they can possibly be.”

He added: “I think that we really need to look at ways that we can really adopt all of that as fast as possible to ease this next stage of growth.”

Eberhard, whose organization advocates for household electrification, also said that while the surge in data center energy demand has spurred a new urgency to the modernization cause, it has also created an environment where industries are ready to try new things. 

“I feel like this era of AI and load growth is a very improv era,” Eberhard said. “There’s a lot of yes-and-ing going on. So yes, we need more transmission lines. Yes, we need more centralized power plants, and we also need to make sure that we’re taking advantage of all this other stuff that we had previously been leaving on the table when we didn’t have this urgency of the AI demand.”

title: Instagram tests ‘Features’ long-form videos, but missing YouTube’s ad share for now
snippet: Instagram is launching “Features” as its first real dive into long-form video content in what could be a real rival to YouTube, though Instagram is, for now, missing an alternative to YouTube’s ad share setup for creators. more…
fullText:
Instagram is launching “Features” as its first real dive into long-form video content in what could be a real rival to YouTube, though Instagram is, for now, missing an alternative to YouTube’s ad share setup for creators.

In a 6-minute video shared today, Instagram head Adam Mosseri and VP Tessa Lyons explain “Features,” a new effort to bring long-form, horizontal video content to Instagram. “Features” allow creators to expand on content in Reels, using short-form video to build up an audience for longer-form content. 

Mosseri explains:

Sat down with @tessalyonsss to talk about why we’re investing in longer videos, which we’re going to call Features, and how they fit with Reels, Series, Live and TV. It’s early, and we’re testing and listening to feedback as we go. But we’re excited to give creators more room to tell their stories with the communities they’ve already built here. More to come.

The video starts with Mosseri admitting that he’s been “against doing long-form video on Instagram,” but the two go on to explain how the trend of friends watching Reels together, including on TV apps, pushed towards this expansion to long-form, horizontal content. Examples of podcast or comedy clips being used in Reels with longer episodes or specials available on “Features” is mentioned, with the two formats being able to connect to each other. 

	

The Hollywood Reporter adds that this is US-only to start – the announcement video can’t even be viewed outside of the US, we found – and also that Instagram will carry over “existing ad deals” with creators.

A lack of any mention around ad sharing programs on Instagram’s part immediately flooded the comments of the announcement, with users asking why they should post long-form videos on Instagram when YouTube pays creators for the same practice. Tessa Lyons says that Instagram thinks “there’s a big opportunity for us to help creators who don’t yet have that infrastructure and that business behind them,” but made no mention of a program like YouTube offers.

title: Spotify confirms it won’t stop Family Plan sharing verification, but it’s not a ‘crackdown’
snippet: Earlier this week a new method of Spotify Family plan verification came to light and, in its latest earnings call, Spotify says that it’s not a “crackdown,” but also something that doesn’t have an “end date.” more…
fullText:
Earlier this week a new method of Spotify Family plan verification came to light and, in its latest earnings call, Spotify says that it’s not a “crackdown,” but also something that doesn’t have an “end date.”

Like virtually every family sharing subscription, Spotify requires Family Plan members to be in the same physical household, but the music streaming app has been looser in its requirements and enforcement. A new method, though, started popping up recently in the form of a verification QR code that makes it a bit more difficult for remote participants to complete verification, and also threatens to ban users from Family plans for a full year if verification isn’t completed.

Spotify’s ‘QR code verification’ cracks down on sharing and could ban you for a year

Today, Spotify’s Q3 earnings call included a question about Spotify “beginning to crack down on Family Plan subscribers that do not live in the same home.” 

Responding to this, Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström says that this is not a “crackdown,” but a “routine improvement of our verification methods,” and something that Spotify will continue to work on. “This is not something that has an end date,” he said:

	

…this is not as much a crackdown as it is actually a routine improvement of our verification methods for our Family Plan. Family Plan has existed for a long while. It has been around for, I think it is now close to 12, 13 years in Spotify history, and it makes up a pretty significant proportion of our subscriber base. As such, it is important for us to just make sure over time that we improve the verification methods that we have. There are certainly ways, over time, to find holes around it. As that happens, we figure out how to improve it over time. This is not something that has an end date. This is not an implementation that is going to complete. This is just ongoing routine.

Reading between the lines, this is saying that Spotify isn’t going to be backing down from verification methods on its Family Plan sharing. QR codes are only the latest implementation.

title: The Latest Echo Smart Speakers Double as Nanny Cams and Wi-Fi Extenders
snippet: Amazon’s new Echo Dot and Studio speakers have several smart home features new to the lineup.
fullText:
Amazon dropped a flurry of new and updated smart home devices today, including its first-ever smart frame and an alarm clock that apparently knows when you’re in a deep sleep and automatically snoozes the alarm until your slumber lightens. 

At the heart of the Echo smart speaker lineup are the Echo Dot, which brings simple smart home convenience, and the Echo Studio, Amazon’s premium listening speaker with a richer sound. Both received big upgrades: The Dot now includes a built-in smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender, while a new Studio adds a camera for live in-home monitoring.

We got a sneak peek at the new smart home speakers at Amazon’s launch event.David Carnoy/CNET

The Studio is the first Echo smart speaker with a camera

Cameras are making their way into products they have no logical business being in, like dishwashers, but a camera in the $250 Echo Studio with Home Camera turns the humble smart speaker into a useful nanny cam, letting you keep tabs on family and pets via its live view. If you’re deciding between a pet cam and a smart speaker, the Echo device should offer a reliable version of both.

			

More from CNET

You can still buy the Echo Studio without a camera for $220.

The cam does more than let you watch the dog chew slippers 

The Studio Home Camera serves as a nanny cam and uses adaptive vision to help with small tasks.David Carnoy/CNET

Through the Home Camera, Alexa “gains visual intelligence to make everyday experiences more personal and helpful,” according to Amazon. Alexa can “see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help. Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”

Adaptive sound and volume for tailored listening

Camera shamera, the Echo Studio also has fancy new audio features.David Carnoy/CNET

Expect the same souped-up sound quality that Studio built its name on, including a high-excursion woofer for deep, immersive bass, three optimally placed full-range drivers, and Dolby Atmos to fill the room with immersive spatial audio. 

	

			

	

			

									

						The Best Smart Speakers We Tested					

							

		

A new feature called Advanced Room Adaptation adjusts the sound to your space’s unique acoustics, while Adaptive Volume adjusts the volume based on how close or far you are from the device. The latter sounds particularly useful for those of us who doddle about the house cooking and cleaning while trying to follow a podcast or audiobook.

Echo Dot is now a smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender

The smaller Echo Dot gets its own updates, including a smart home hub feature and a built-in Wi-Fi extender. 

For the first time, Amazon has integrated a smart home hub to connect and control compatible devices like your smart thermostat, lights and locks without the need for a standalone hub. The latest iteration adds a built-in Eero Wi-Fi extender that extends internet coverage by up to 1,000 square feet to an existing Eero network. 

For the first time, the Echo Dot features a built-in smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender.David Carnoy/CNET

Echo Dot is now powered by AZ3, Amazon’s custom-designed silicon, enabling advanced on-device

processing for faster, more natural conversations with Alexa Plus. Speaking of Alexa, there’s now a fourth speaker (all the better to hear you with, my dear).

Echo Dot and Studio pricing

Echo Studio with Home Camera is $249.99 and available in Graphite. An optional stand is sold separately for $39.99

Echo Dot is available in Graphite, Glacier White, Agave Green, and Coral Pink for $99.99.

Amazon Kids Echo Dot is available in two colorful designs – Octopus and Penguin – starting at $109.99

title: Who’s really in charge at Anthropic after the IPO?
snippet: Here's a clear explanation of Anthropic's incredibly complex governance structure.
fullText:
Anthropic was founded in 2021 to ensure humanity can control AI and benefit from it in the long-term. As the frontier lab approaches its initial public offering, however, there’s one class of humanity that is being shut out of control: anyone who buys its stock on public markets.

Complex structures that allow founders like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg to control their public companies without owning most of them are nothing new in Silicon Valley. But Anthropic’s obsession with AI safety has resulted in a truly baroque style of corporate governance that will leave common shareholders with little say over most major decisions at the AI company, including who sits on its board.

First, Anthropic is a public benefit company — a for-profit corporation legally allowed to weigh a public mission alongside profit — with the goal of promoting AI safety. That status protects the board’s ability to make decisions about AI safety that aren’t driven entirely by shareholder value without being sued by angry investors.

Right now, the board is chaired by Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and includes CEO Dario Amodei (her brother), Netflix cofounder Reed Hastings, former Microsoft and GM CFO Christopher Liddell, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, and Spark Capital partner Yasmin Razavi. There is one vacancy on the board.

Second, Anthropic has allocated significant control of its board to a Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), an independent panel meant to keep the company focused on mission to benefit humanity. The trust owns a class of stock that gives it the ability to elect and remove a majority of the company’s board, known as Class T directors. The LTBT is chaired by Neil Shah, a global health expert who was managing director at GiveWell, a nonprofit that ranks charities, and includes former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke, national security expert Richard Fontaine, and Harvard physicist Christopher Stubbs. There is one vacancy on the LTBT right now. The existing members will themselves choose who fills it.

Third, Anthropic’s seven founders also jointly own a special class of stock that gives a majority of them 50.1% of shareholder voting power, allowing them to elect three members of the board of directors. If, for whatever reason, there’s no majority among the founders, only then are their shares voted in proportion with holders of common stock.

Finally, the board can put a check on the LTBT. When the LTBT nominates a “Specified” one of its four directors, or removes that director without cause (that is, without alleging misconduct), the board’s nominating committee can decline to approve the move and throw the decision to the company’s employees for a vote.

Here’s what all that looks like:

Image Credits:Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch

The dynamics of such a complex structure are hard to predict. We’ve already seen one notable instance where a similar structure was essentially overthrown: OpenAI’s so-called blip, when OpenAI’s board briefly fired CEO Sam Altman over concerns that he was not being candid with them. Thanks to the loyalty of the company’s employees to Altman, the board backed down, reinstated him, and a new governance structure was put in place. Anthropic’s structure seems to formalize that kind of employee power.

At Anthropic, cracks in the founders’ unified front could lead to common shareholders having more say than expected, while employees can overrule the LTBT on board seats if they back the board over the assembled luminaries.

The founders’ control won’t last forever: Ten years after the IPO, the founders can choose to end their control of the company, or their control will end automatically when fewer than three of them remain. At that point, the LTBT will continue until 85% of common shareholders vote to end it, or it decides to step down with approval from the board. 

If and when neither special class of shareholder exists any more — hopefully not because of an AI-driven catastrophe — common shareholders finally get control.

title: Supernatural, the best VR workout app, makes its glorious comeback today
snippet: Supernatural made a name for itself as the de facto workout app through the COVID era and beyond, and is coming back from the grave as an independent app, starting today. more…
fullText:
Supernatural made a name for itself as the de facto workout app through the COVID era and beyond, and is coming back from the grave as an independent app, starting today.

Workout trends often come and go like the wind, but a few staples hang around long enough to be properly cemented into the “this really works” category. Supernatural is one such example. The VR workout app debuted on April 23, 2020, making it the best way to get a gym-like workout in a world where all the gyms were shut down during the pandemic. Lots of people used it and continued to use it until earlier this year, when Meta closed the studio that made it.

People were devastated. The entire Supernatural community on Facebook was up in arms. But it wasn’t long until Supernatural’s founders announced that they had acquired the rights and would be returning later in 2026 as an independent company, and today is that day.

Meta Quest 3 at Amazon

AMVR FC4M magnetic face pad (you’ll thank me later) at Amazon

Supernatural Early Access is officially launching today, October 21, on Meta’s storefront. You can get a free 7-day trial by downloading the app, and then it’s $20 per month after that. An extended 14-day free trial is available to folks who sign up for the $200/year plan, which grants a $40 annual discount by paying up front.

	

If you haven’t used Supernatural before, you’re about to be very pleasantly surprised. The game features daily coach-led workouts with popular music you’ll love to work out to. Gamers move their bodies around to the beat, smashing flying obstacles with bats, ducking, kicking, and generally getting very sweaty. The whole thing takes place in incredibly realistic environments, which the Supernatural team says are getting a big visual upgrade in the new release.

Today’s early access version launches with thousands of workouts available immediately — with all the coaches you know and love — including hundreds of licensed music tracks, a brand new home environment set in Laguna Torre, a glacial lake in Argentine Patagonia, and the ability to transfer your entire workout history from the old Supernatural app to the new one. I know my colleague, Daniel Bader, will be very happy about that.

Founding members will start with a custom bat, and more rewards are dropping throughout the early access period. Additionally, household accounts can be used to share the experience with up to four people in your home, including individual profiles for each one. Make sure you get a good face pad that’s easy to clean if you do this!

As Supernatural continues to get rebuilt and gets better than ever, users can expect more workouts and music on a weekly cadence, the return of real-time workouts with friends (sign up for the beta now), a new mobile companion app (that pairs with your smartwatch), new destinations, and plenty of rewards for returning and founding members. It’s incredible, and it’s quite frankly mind-blowing to see the entire team return this way, all without the help of Meta.

title: Google Maps on CarPlay rolling out Gemini when navigating
snippet: Google Maps in CarPlay now lets you access Gemini when navigating for a conversational driving experience. more…
fullText:
Google Maps in CarPlay now lets you access Gemini when navigating for a conversational driving experience.

	

When using navigation, tapping the Gemini icon on the right edge lets you ask multi-step questions and issue commands like:

“What park is famous for gorgeous views overlooking the city?”

“I want to go at a time when it’s not too busy and the weather will stay nice. Is now a good time?”

“Start navigating me there but make sure to avoid toll roads.”

This is the first time Google Maps is offering voice assistant functionality in CarPlay. Previously, Google Assistant was only available when using Google Maps navigation directly on your iPhone.

Gemini can also be used to report traffic disruptions with your voice. This matches the navigation experience introduced on Google Maps for Android and iOS last year, while it’s already available in Android Auto.

	

Gemini in Google Maps on Apple CarPlay is available now in the US, while the global rollout is underway.

title: Apple responds to reports of iPhone Duo’s inner display cracking
snippet: Over the weekend, a handful of iPhone Duo users reported that their inner display had cracked along the hinge. In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said it is “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” and that affected users can contact AppleCare for a replacement. more…
fullText:
Over the weekend, a handful of iPhone Duo users reported that their inner display had cracked along the hinge. In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said it is “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” and that affected users can contact AppleCare for a replacement. 

Here is Apple’s full statement: 

“The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor. We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.”

The company says the problem affects a very small number of iPhone Duo units and appears to surface relatively quickly. Most iPhone Duo units are not affected. You do not need AppleCare+ to have your iPhone Duo replaced for this problem. If you bought from a carrier, you should contact AppleCare directly, not your carrier, to get your device replaced. 

Reports of the problem surfaced on Reddit and other forums over the weekend. Affected users report that the inner screens cracked along the center line of the hinge. While a number of user reports on Reddit showing the issue are legitimate, there have been a handful of fake AI-generated reports as well. 

The folks at iFixit have pointed to a few potential causes of the problems, with certain components potentially putting excessive pressure on the display.

title: Apple’s low-cost iPhone 18 details revealed by leaker
snippet: Apple reportedly plans to introduce a low-cost iPhone 18e next spring alongside iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Here are the details on what to expect from iPhone 18e, per a new leak. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly plans to introduce a low-cost iPhone 18e next spring alongside iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Here are the details on what to expect from iPhone 18e, per a new leak.

iPhone 18e will feature A20 chip and possible front camera upgrade, but remain very similar to iPhone 17e per leaker

When Apple introduced new iPhones last month, only three models launched: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, plus iPhone Duo.

Rumors indicate three more new iPhones are coming in early 2027: iPhone 18e, iPhone 18, and iPhone Air 2.

There’s been plenty of reporting on iPhone Air 2 changes, and some on the base iPhone 18, but surprisingly little on the entry-model iPhone 18e.

But today, a new post from Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station outlines what to expect from iPhone 18e early next year. He says it will feature:

60Hz display, meaning no ProMotion still

A20 chip, which doesn’t yet exist in non-Pro form

6.12-inch OLED like its predecessor

48MP single rear camera

Front camera “may be upgraded to 24MP”

Based on these specs, it sounds like iPhone 18e is focused largely on performance improvements.

The A20 chip will be interesting to evaluate, since we haven’t yet seen a non-Pro variant of the latest 2nm technology. Mention of a front camera upgrade is particularly surprising, but my guess is that if it does emerge, it will actually be an 18MP sensor like what’s in other models today.

Other than these two changes, every spec mentioned remains unchanged from iPhone 17e. One detail not addressed is whether the notch will be replaced by a Dynamic Island.

Considering the skyrocketing prices of memory and storage, and Apple’s aims to keep iPhone 18e a budget-friendly model, perhaps the new model will offer fewer upgrades than usual to keep costs down.

title: OnePlus starts rolling out stable Android 17 updates early, marking the end of OxygenOS
snippet: OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS. more…
fullText:
OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS.

OxygenOS has been OnePlus’ skin on top of Android for years. It started off as a “stock” skin with some added features, but eventually transitioned into a global-optimized version of Oppo’s ColorOS. So it wasn’t a surprise that, when OnePlus shut down most of its global operations, it was also announced that OxygenOS would go away with existing devices updating to ColorOS. 

Starting in India, ColorOS 17 based on Android 17 is rolling out to the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4. The update has been in beta for a while now, but today marks the start of the stable rollout.

OnePlus summarizes ColorOS 17, saying:

	

ColorOS 17 is here, bringing a new wave of smarter experiences, smoother interactions, and more ways to make your phone work around you… At the heart of ColorOS 17 is an idea we believe in: Flow with AI, Flow Everywhere. Technology should feel less like something you have to figure out and more like something that naturally keeps up with you. From making everyday interactions feel more fluid to turning ideas into finished work with AI, we’re bringing intelligence closer to the moments that matter, helping you move between tasks, devices, and experiences with less friction.

Originally, OnePlus’ timeline put the first updates on October 29.

Other devices confirmed to be updated include last-gen flagships and an assortment of Nord devices, but OnePlus 15 and Pad 4 are the only two for this first wave. Presumably, the update will expand to other regions in the coming days. The next wave lands on October 30 and includes OnePlus 13.
